reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing turtle experience!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had heard that there were a number of sea turtles coming ashore every evening, so we decided to check it out.  We did not expect 30+ huge individuals.As we watched, they continued to come ashore.   Very quick until they hit the sand - then you could see the struggle.  Simply amazing.  Area around the turtles was marked off with red tape.  People were very respectful. Plenty of parking available along the street.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped this beach while touring Kauai.  The weather wasn’t very nice to swimming wasn’t really an option, although it looked like it would be a nice spot in the right conditions.  The waves were quite large outside of the cove.  This highlight were the turtles.  There were at least 25-30 large turtles resting on the beach.  That’s the most we’ve seen in any one place.  This area is definitely worth visiting.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: So many turtles!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When we got to the beach midday there were 18 turtles on the beach. We decided to drive back to our nearby hotel to grab our snorkeling gear. Came back and there were 40 turtles on the beach. Incredible!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowd-central
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While this is certainly a scenic spot, the crowds we experienced over the holidays made it unpleasant. It might be better in the low season. Parking was tough and it was like being at a concert in terms of crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The sleeping turtles are magical
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was lovely to watch the sunrise and get to experience the nightly/early rotation of sea turtles who call that beach their home outside the water. *As a friendly reminder for all that go to see the turtles and other wildlife there… please don’t act entitled. There are beautiful kind volunteers who give their time to protect the turtles space. This is for THEIR safety. Don’t be rude to them, if they tell you that you are too close (walking inside their cone barriers) politely apologize and step back. They don’t deserve to be yelled at. They are doing the work so we can to view and be in company of amazing animals. It breaks my heart to witness tourists who think they are entitled to a picture so close to the animal and then yell at the volunteers who politely ask them to step away. Use your camera zoom and don’t be a jerk please!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had an awesome time on the beach areas. In hindsight, you could park at the main parking area and hit several locations along the Poipu Beach area. You can swim, boogie board, and see the turtles all in one day. I don't recommend eating near the beach because it is very expensive. Take snacks and treat yourself to an early dinner in  Old Koloa Town.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach on Kauai ...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Super easy to walk to. Plenty of space to set your chair down and enjoy a morning, afternoon or day at the beach. Surf is good for young kids to play and more than good enough for great boogy boarding or body surfing. Spot the sea turtles in the surf or at sunset check them and seals out on the beach. If you have patience, scan the ocean horizon, you will definitely see whale activity ... Spouts, tails and breeching. Enjoy!!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles everywhere, just amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A great place to see the Hawaii green Sea turtles. They are all around and just napping on the beach among people. Its a beautiful and large beach with plenty of space to hangout with the turtles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach of the south shore of the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the best beaches on the island. Great mix of beach, wild life, surf. What is special are the 20+ turtles who come swim out on the beach. We Sally see sea lions but not this time. Only tough part of the beach - tough to get in and out of the water due to the rocks

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Turtles, waves, sun, sand, boogie boarding, and all within walking distance of several hotels and condominiums available for rent.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: 10/10 Would Recommend
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a great beach to watch the turtles. There were lots of people but it didnt feel crowded. Also a great place to catch the sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go For The Turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This popular beach is located in the south part of Kauai. It is known for being a beautiful beach with great swimming. There are two lifeguard stands staffed with lifeguards. There is ample parking which is not always a thing with some of the beaches on Kauai. Our favorite thing about this beach is when the green sea turtles come up on shore to rest. It is quite a site to see. The area around the turtles is protected by a series of cones with signs telling visitors to stay back and to leave the turtles alone. While we were there, everyone was very respectful and did not cross the boundary.The beach is clearly marked from the main road and easy to find. There is a restaurant right on the beach so if you need something to eat or drink, you can do so without having to leave.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Aloha
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The turtles were so amazing - they come up to sleep every night. Any where from 1-50- not joking!!! Be respectful. Across the street is puka dogs, it was yummy

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Well designed beach park with something for all ages!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Quite a lovely place with grass, covered picnic area & water  suitable for toddlers up to snorklers!  We were staying almost next door at Waiohai Beach Club so it was a 5 minute beach stroll from our home base, often  strewn with monk seals and green sea turtles every day of our stay. Visitors were respecting the resting wild life and the dedicated volunteers were kept busy by the frequently moving turtles and seals. The most turtles seen at one time by various family members were 72 sea turtles after sunset one evening!  In the early hours after 7AM,  usually only a few, but Brenneke’s coffee and bakery shop across the street is open early for pleasant beach snack at the picnic benches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Place To Eat Your Puka Dog On The Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We sat at one of the picnic benches in this park to eat our Puka Dog, which I highly recommend.  There is a big pavilion and picnic tables scattered around.  Most have shade, so do not. We had no issue grabbing a table this time of year.  We sat and ate and enjoyed the sounds of ocean for about 25 minutes. There is a playground for kids and a public restroom also available.  The beach itself was not to crowded considering to is in close proximity to lots of hotels & resorts. We were there early afternoon so we missed the turtles coming up onto the beach.  You could see where they rope off for the turtles to try to keep tourist from getting to close.We did find an old pay phone booth that still had the phones in the booth! I thought that was pretty fun!  The park itself is nice, the beach is beautiful but busy.  We did walk to the other side of the beach where it was very rocky.  Also beautiful here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunsets and turtles amidst white sand and clear waters
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of my favorite beaches in Kauai. This is one of the best places to see the sunset if you’re near the south or eastern side of Kauai. If you come during sunset, you’ll get a chance to see the sea turtles come with the waves to rest for the evening. Although you can’t get close to them, you can go snorkeling in the water just don’t touch the animals. If you have any questions about them, there are local volunteers protecting and answering any questions people have about the turtles.Also, there is a parking lot across the street so come early to find the best parking. During sunset besides turtles, you’ll see surfers, riding the waves. One of the best sunsets of my life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach and Water Aerobics Class
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Love this beach. Great soft sand. A great place to see turtles and monk seals. There is nothing better than getting your beach chairs and parasol and relaxing on the beach. Great to watch the surfers. The ocean is so warm and a great place to cool off. However the best for me is Charlotte’s water aerobics class in the ocean held on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings at 9am.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkeling and Turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach. It had excellent snorkeling from the beach. Lots of colorful fish. Also when we were there, there were lots of turtles on land. It was cool to see them. We went mid-morning and didnt have a problem finding parking. They do have bathrooms but they were quite disgusing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: People are indifferent and cruel towards animals
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We were there today and it was honestly kind of disgusting how people were acting around the beach. They seemed to be keeping an okay distance from the turtles and there were several volunteers answering questions. My main concern here is that we witnessed someone run over and kill a young chicken. They immediately left and it had seizures/convulsions(?) until it died. We told a shop owner and he said no one cares about the chickens. Our waiter at dinner told us not to mourn the chicken and that it didn’t matter at all. Probably 30 minutes later, we saw 4 people put a rooster into a garbage can and shake it until the rooster starting crying.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Bring water shoes, trust me, it will make your experience so much nicer
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If I could offer one piece of advise, its to BRING WATER SHOES.  I'm so glad we had them in the car.  The entrance into the water is rocky with lots of divots. I observed lots of people entering the water with their arms spread, trying to balance themselves from falling.    Once we put on the water shoes, it was a lot easier to get in.    The water was crystal clear and the snorkeling is fantastic.  I saw more fish here than I saw on our snorkeling expedition.  There are 2 lifeguards who are continuously telling people to "not mess with the wildlife" and to move in closer".  I felt super safe here.   When we were here, there was a large turtle who was making its way to the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach but watch out for theft
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful snorkeling beach.  Tons of fish, pretty shallow water.  Park has lifeguards, restrooms, showers, a playground and plenty of free parking.  The issue is we were robbed. There is a concrete wall in the back of the park, its guarding a cemetery.  We put our two bags next to the wall and when we came back our bookbag was taken and rummaged through. Our bag was dropped a short distance away. We didn't have anything of value in our bags but you have to be careful of this area even on a busy beach day.   Just a reminder to leave valuables at home or in the car and enjoy this beautiful beach.  🤙

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great amenities and beautiful beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was beautiful. It’s a park with amenities, so expect more of a crowd than other beaches in Kauai. We tried snorkeling but there were others who had the same idea. We enjoyed lounging on the beach and listening to the waves.Look for the green turtles who are sunbathing. They are in a protected area and easy to find.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing day at the beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu beach is one of Kauai's south beaches! Dry and sunny all day. It's nestled with resorts and condos. Parking is fantastic and free, close to the beach. The park has showers to clean off the sand and bathroom. It also has picnic shelters. Thinner beaches with lifeguards, the beach drops off and has rocks all over. The current is dangerous so please listen to the lifeguards.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cozy, family friendly and easily accessible
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Small but popular, wonderful beach with golden sugar-soft sand. Unique touch are the sea turtles and monk seals who occasionally rest here- we saw both! For these reasons it drew me back for multiple visits- the easily accessible parking also helps. The signs carefully mark where the safe areas to swim are; there are powerful currents not too far so beware especially with children. The snorkeling is not bad (especially with the turtles), but the waves and surf can make it a little challenging.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with turtles and snorkelling opportunities, but watch the currents!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a nice family beach where turtles come and  sunbathe. It has life guards and they are on the ball looking after peoples safety with changing tides and strong currents. There are covered / shaded picnic tables, toilets and changing rooms and a free car park nearby.  There are coral reefs where people can snorkel and see tropical fish. The currents are strong so you need to be a competent swimmer and use fins. Big Al’s top tipsIf snorkelling come in the morning as the water is clearer and less murky. Use fins as the currents can be strong A good place to see turtles and free car parking toilet / changing rooms . One of the nicest beaches on the island and well worth a visit. Follow me for more travel tips around the world.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty Views at Poipu Beach Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you're staying on the south side of Kaua'i, you will be familiar with Poipu Beach Park by day one.  It's a public beach with many places to relax, rocky points to search for sea life, and all around incredible views (especially those sunsets).If you're looking for a more private beach, this won't be it as it's a public beach for locals and tourists alike.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful, fun beach with sea turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was beautiful and there were at least 6 sea turtles on the beach in the late afternoon. There is a rock cove that is protected from the surf so you can swim and snorkel without worrying about the stronger tide.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointed
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Way crowded and rough waters. The rocky ocean floor tore up my kids' feet and knees. We literally left bloody. Apparently there are 2 sides to this beach - the one for surfing and the one for families. Yes, we were on the correct, calmer side. It was awful. The good thing about this beach is there are clean bathrooms and changing rooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice big beach park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I have been here many times to watch turtles and to swim. The calm side of the beach is usually pretty crowded - especially when the turtles are arriving or sleeping. Parking is plentiful and free.  It is easy to access and a good beach for swimming.  Poipu Beach is really two beaches because it is split into two sides. Once side has a shallow snorkeling and swinning area that seems pretty good for new snorkelers or kids. The other side is not as calm and a lot of sand for sunning.  The beach is within walking distance to Brennecke's Beach that seems to be the exclusive territory for surfers. The park itself contains showers, restrooms, and plenty of picnic tables and abuts each side of Poipu and Brennecke beaches.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for snorkeling & decompressing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a recommendation & it did not disappoint. There was plenty of room for small & larger groups, including further down the beach.  At the time (a May weekday 2025), parking was getting sparse across the street, yet there wasn't a line on the street looking for a spot.  We also found a business that rented umbrellas & chairs all day for a reasonable price. If you can't find a spot on the beach to sit, there is a grass area with picnic tables within close proximity to the water. Aside from the black crabs on the rocks & the sea turtles coming ashore. snorkeling seemed popular with some decent results.  Outside of the inlet was good surfing waves.I can't guarantee what happens on the weekend, holidays, or during warmer weather with the crowds, but if you can be here on a weekday, it might be better

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with lifeguard
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent a little while here enjoying the warm sea, the turtles basking and the children enjoying the sea.   Shallow sea where there is a lifeguard on duty.   Sadly we had to leave in a hurry owing to a massive downpour but would’ve happily stayed longer just enjoying watching people enjoying life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: We went twice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Turtles are an amazing sight to see! Respect them, watch the signs, WATCH YOUR CHILDREN, and give them space. Beach is packed

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtle & Monk Seal Viewing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Thanks to a volunteer at the beach who had a flashlight with a red light, saw 50 turtles sleeping  on the beach and rocks one night (volunteers count the turtles about every hour).  Went back for sunrise two days later and saw turtles wake up and slowly crawl back into the water.  Also saw a monk seal swim ashore to sleep.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: #50thfor50 Fun!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was amazing! We saw turtles resting on the sandy beach. Two monk seals came ashore to play right in front of us! The shore was rocky in places.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: See the turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the famed sea turtle beach. Every day, around sunset, green sea turtles come out onto the beach for some rest. The turtle zone is cordoned off, but you can still get quite close. We did not go in the water, but there were several snorkelers when we were there and apparently you can see other turtles while you are snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Getting close to see life
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If I could give it more I would.  Up close and personal with turtles and monk seals.  Water was calm and beautiful. Slightly over crowded in the afternoon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Family Beach with Basking Protected Sea Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice park and a great spot for Sunset and the Sea Turtles.  If you have kids there is a terrific place where the kids can wallow in the shallow water, and if the kids are a little older, there is a spot where they can learn to snorkel to the right of the turtles.  What you do need to know is that part of the beach is dedicated to the basking sea turtles.  This is the ONLY spot in the world where the sea turtles rest on the beach daily.  There are there pretty much all day long, but start to come into the beach around sunset and leave around sunrise.  Watch out for parking challenges around sunset, since this is the prime place to catch sunset in Poipu.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtle Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is the best beach! Very shallow- you can walk out and still be waist deep. It's good to have water shoes. Snorkel is amazing, AND after lunch, the turtles come in to take a nap on the beach! I could watch this all day long!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles and Monk Seals!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lucky to see 24 sea turtles on the beach and monk seals sunbathing.  The beach is crowded and not my favorite to relax but the turtles and sea lions made it worth it.  I could have watched them all afternoon.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Perfect place to end our day w some snorkeling and boogie boarding with a sunset that speaks for it's self. A walk up var right there. Don't know what else to ask for

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see while in Kauai
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach is clean with restrooms. There are food options near by. There were 3 large Hawaiian Green Turtles onshore, amazing creatures!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Love this Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our favorite beach in Kauai.  The beach is family friendly but the surf is still too rough for novice swimmers.  Snorkelers will enjoy seeing plentiful tropical fish near the shore in the protected cove.  The beach frequently has resting green sea turtles and Hawaiian munk seals on the shore sunbathing (they are protected, with the area immediately around them roped off to keep visitors from disturbing them).  There is free parking across the street for those who are not staying in one of the nearby resorts or condos.  Water shoes are recommended if you want to wade in the water due to the rocks and uneven bottom, although there are a few sandy water entry points.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots of turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I sat here for over an hour watching the sunset and watching all the turtles come in. It was cool to see and the beach and water look nice for young families too as the water looked calmer. Started at 12 turtles and ended up with 28 before we left and I imagine more were coming in, they say they get up to 50 normally according to local volunteers there protecting the turtles so people don’t get too close.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Kauai Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach- was able toSit comfortably from mid afternoon til sundown watching the waves, surfers, seals, turtles, and whales! It was clean, lifeguards made it safe, and a time well-spent, snorkeling, swimming, sunning and sun-setting!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Turtles are the Thing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A bit crowded but the turtles are the thing.  We visited during lunch time to try the hot dog place and were surprised to see a turtle coming up the beach - everyone gets so excited to see these creatures!  Our 3-yr old was mesmerized and wanted to come back that evening- when dozens were sleeping on the beach. So go for the turtles - and sometimes the seals will be there too - but go other places to get away from crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles and Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Awesome beach with snorkeling and where turtles come on beach to sleep at night after 5:30 PM.If you are there just for turtles arrive around 5 PM and you can watch them swim in.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful scenery
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous beach with stunning sunrise and sunset photo opportunities. Can get a little crowded. Lifeguards and bathrooms on site

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not Great Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Underwhelming Snorkeling at Poipu Beach ParkPoipu Beach Park is a lovely spot for relaxing by the water, but the snorkeling experience left a lot to be desired. The water here is incredibly shallow, making it difficult to move around without worrying about hitting the coral or stirring up sand. This really took away from the enjoyment of exploring the underwater scenery.Additionally, the area was extremely crowded, with swimmers and snorkelers everywhere. It was hard to find space to enjoy the experience without bumping into others. The congestion made it feel more chaotic than relaxing.While the park itself is beautiful, I wouldn’t recommend it if your primary goal is snorkeling. There are definitely better spots on the island for a more enjoyable and peaceful underwater adventure.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to snorkel and swim with turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Did not snorkel at the beach since we ended up on the wrong beach down the road.  But we made it in enough time at Dusk when the Turtles come ashore to bask overnight.  Turtles are swimming just offshore along with other fish.  You're not allowed to touch or get near the turtle, but you can get very close to you.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Poipu Beach State Park: Paradise with Precautions for turtles and sharks at twilight.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is undeniably gorgeous, but like all natural wonders, it demands respect. While generally safe, families with young children should be extra cautious, especially after 4 pm.Why? * Turtles:  Green sea turtles graze in the shallows during late afternoons. They're gentle but have strong jaws that can accidentally bite curious little hands. * Sharks:  As daylight fades, sharks may venture closer to shore to hunt. While attacks are rare, vigilance is key, especially with small children.Stay safe: * Supervise closely:  Never leave young children unattended in the water, particularly in the late afternoon. * Respect wildlife:  Teach kids to admire turtles from afar, not approach them. * Clear water is key:  Avoid murky water or areas with schooling fish, as these attract sharks. * Lifeguard wisdom:  Always heed posted warnings and lifeguard advice.Enjoy Poipu's beauty, but prioritize safety, especially for your little ones. A bit of awareness ensures a memorable and worry-free visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Can be done if you like crowded beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Too crowded for my personal taste. Clean beach. Lifeguard, showers, lots of parking spaces are available. There were about 10 sea turtles lying on the beach sunbathing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: JUST BEACHY!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with plenty of parking, picnic areas, swimming area with lifeguards.  We saw monk seals and sea turtles!  Docents are there to answer questions about the sea life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach. Lots of sand and grass as well. Turtles visit every evening to nest. Lifeguards stand At one end as well as park rangers to tell about the turtles and keep them safe.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favorite beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove all over the island and this ended up being our favorite beach, it was close to our rental house, we could watch the turtles come in at night, the sand was glorious, sunsets beautiful, snorkeling was incredible, and usually a monk seal would be snoozing nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely beach area with lifeguards, bathrooms, picnic tables and some shade.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed the morning relaxing, snorkeling and swimming at Poipu beach.  Large swimming area was very rocky on the bottom so bring water shoes.  The kiddie swimming area was sandy instead of rocky but was pretty shallow for snorkeling, although many people were doing so.  Saw many of one type of fish, about 6-9 inches long.  (Saw more at Lydgate the day before without snorkle gear).  We came back later in the afternoon and hung around to watch the turtles move onto the beach from the water.  Saw 5 turtles and then headed back to resort.  It was a beautiful sunny, hot day and the beach was crowded but there is a huge, free parking area and people seem to come and go regularly and parking is not an issue.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Our favorite beach on that side of the island…read to learn more about what to expect!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was such a find for us! We started at the beach in front of the Sheraton and it was a bit rough for us to be honest! We were staying at the Koloa Landing Resort (check out my in depth review on that incredible Marriott Autograph Collection property) so we had access to umbrella rentals, etc. but we were looking for novice level seas, some snorkeling, swimming, that sort of thing. Our hotel recommended Poipu Beach and it was only a short, 4 minute drive by car and there is also a path to walk to it if you want.First, get there early for parking! Second, bring shade if you need it unless you plan to sit under the canopy with picnic tables. It’s nice, but it’s a bit back from the beach. We rented an umbrella and although it got windy, our umbrella worked out great!There is an active lifeguard tower and they are working hard to keep folks safe. Although there is a protected area to swim, there is also a section where the tides converge and they were constantly monitoring and using the megaphone to tell folks to come back in. There is a cute little island just across the way and there were plenty of fish to see! We even saw them right up my close to the shore! And if you get lucky, you will see a turtle or two on the shore as it is mating season now and we saw 3 large turtles out there! Also, there is a place near the shaded picnic tables to spray yourself off, I just did not see any restrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Disappointed - too crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It was unfortunately completely crowded. I suppose the interest is to see turtles, but you have to be ready to be very near other families and people to do so.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: See Sea Turtles!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The sea turtles come on to the beach to sleep at night.  Be sure to go see them in the evening before it gets dark.  We went about 6:15. You will see them swimming in and climbing onto the beach. Volunteers are there to make sure everyone keeps their distance from the turtles.  There is a nice parking lot with a short walk to the turtles. They are on the beach end near Brenneck's Restaurant. Just look for all the people and the orange cones.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: top class beach with great combination of nice beach to relax and reef to explore
reviewsWithKeywords.text: magnificent place. ideal combination of a great beach for those in the family wanting to relax and a reef to explore for those more into adventure. we enjoyed both. top class beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Run of the mill beach experience
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was nice however it was pretty crowded. Lifeguards only allow you to swim out a very short distance . A lot of coral so you definitely need proper swim shoes. You can get drinks from the Marriott bar next door.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to go with the kids to snorkel and see turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We have been here twice during our stay on Kauai and the beach gives nice opportunities to snorkel as well as see turtles live and up close.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This park and beach are fantastic!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our condo was within walking distance. We watched sea turtles come onto the beach at night to sleep. Then we watched them waking in the morning. Saw monk seals napping by the lifeguard stand. One section of the beach is great for body surfing and another is very good for snorkeling.The park itself is just a wonderful, relaxing place to spend the day. Plus Puka Dog is right behind it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Many reasons to go to Poipu Beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Super popular beach, and for good reason!  1. Turtles on the beach!2. Seal on the beach!3. Lifeguard station4. Food nearby5. Public restroom at beach6. Great sunsets!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach to snorkel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is a beautiful area to swim and snorkel.  Lifeguards are on duty and the waves aren’t too strong.  My husband and I snorkeled right off the beach (maybe 30 feet away from the shore), and we saw tons of colorful fish.  You might want to wear water shoes because the bottom of the ocean to get to where people were snorkeling was very rocky and sharp.  The beach is very clean and not too crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: If you love turtles you must come here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came on a Sunday afternoon because I heard a rumour that turtles come up on the beach in the afternoon to sleep and it is true. It was quite busy but that is okay as we came for one reason only. The beach is quite pretty and there were a lot of people snorkelling in the water. I just missed seeing the Monk Seals and when I asked the volunteer if there are turtles, he pointed over and said see those rock looking things, well they are turtles. There are volunteers by the turtles so if you have any questions, they will helpfully answer them for you. I love turtles so I am so happy we came. Oh, and the beach is patrolled if you are considering to swim.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for small children
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent beach for snorkeling albeit very shallow in spots. Great beach for small children since it has a very protected and shallow water area on the left.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkel here, Swim & relax elsewhere
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach to snorkel and it was so cool to see the turtles and monk seal on shore, but not great for swimming.  We did see quite a few different fish while snorkeling. This beach was so talked up about being one of the best, but I found it overcrowded and the rocks and coral made it uncomfortable to be in if you were not interested in snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is a must do on your Kauai vacation!!!  The beach is very large and clean.  There is a great area to surf, snorkel, and swim, and the area is a wonderful place to watch the sunset.But, best of all are the turtles.  Every evening, sea turtles make their way up onto the sand to sleep for the night.  There will be volunteers there roping off the area to to protect them.  The volunteers are friendly and love to answer all of our sea turtle questions.  Early in the morning, the sea turtles will then scoot back into the water to play in the surf.  This beach is also a great place to watch the turtles swim in the water all day.  On our last night there, we also saw 2 monk seals playing in the water and make their way onto the sand at the same time the turtles were coming in.  Once in a lifetime experience, and Poipu Beach will always be on my must-do list when I return to Kauai.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: More than excellent
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu has been rated one of the best beaches in the US. It certainly doesn’t disappoint. To the right of the lifeguard tower is a great place to swim and play in the surf. To the left is shallower, a great place to snorkel. We saw so many different fish, it was awesome. Oh, and we made friends with the Monk Seal’s and Sea Turtles that showed up

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Amazing beach, so many turtles and even a sea lion. Beautiful sand and sunset and a great, safe spot for snorkeling or for kids to swim!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Relaxing in Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful views of the lush green mountains and foliage and the roll of the waves. Enjoy the warm sand as you relax to the sound of the surf.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An exciting experience!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed Poipu beach as we went late in the afternoon to see the turtles we were told about. The park was beautiful with facilities and picnic areas. There was snorkeling in a nice shallow bay and surfers nearby. As the sun started to set, turtles came into the bay and right up on the beach for their evening rest. It was amazing! They have a volunteer conservationist that comes and gives information about the turtles and answers questions. It was a wonderful experience!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: You will likely see turtles and monk seals
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a clean well maintained beach and park.  Snorkeling was easy.  There were large turtles and monk seals resting on the sand and were roped off for their safety.  This seemed to be popular with families since it is well protected.  Parking was easy and a shirt walk across a path.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The Beach I Hate to Love
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is one of those places that I hate to love. It has snorkeling, swimming, body surfing and beach walking that is just wonderful…and there are lots of people. I was fortunate to see two huge endangered monk seals that had beached for a rest. They were protected by naturalists and a fence.  There are some very nice resorts right along the beach where you can go and get a meal or a drink. There are public bathrooms and shelters for having picnic lunch or running under when a quick rain shower appears. The parking lot is large but as I said this is a very popular spot.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: SO fun to see a large sea turtle and a monk seal on the beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove down to Poipu Beach to have a bit more of a relaxed day after doing so many of the touristy sites prior, and this was so enjoyable as although there were many people out on the sand playing in the surf or lying on beach towels, there was plenty of room to walk and to see the water and sites.  We loved seeing a large sea turtle making her way back into the water from a position on the beach where a tape "fence" kept people back from where she was so as not to disturb her at all.  From there, we walked on a bit further where a young monk seal was sleeping on the warm sand!  He, too, had a barrier to prevent anyone from getting too close and disturbing him.  They had a sign up telling his sex as well as when he had come up on the sand to sleep.  Every once in a while, he would raise a flipper or move so we knew he was still alive!  When my husband wanted to walk a little further, I went up to read at a covered picnic table, and watched as a rooster and a female chicken jumped up on the edge of a lined garbage can just a few feet from me to look for food.  I broke out in laughter when the rooster fell INTO the can and I think falling in startled him so badly that there was a rush of fluffy feathers seen in the can before he was able to fly out!  Funny that he didn't come back to try again!  I got pictures of some cardinals with bright red heads as well as other birds coming to the tables to check me and a few other people out for any scraps from meals!  We were told not to feed any of the chickens, but while eating our food at a table, the wind blew our potato chips off the table and onto the ground!!  And the roosters, mama chickens as well as their babies came running!  They got free treats that day because we couldn't gather up the dropped pieces fast enough!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with great snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu was great! It was somewhat windy, but if you sit past the main beach over by the hotel it is protected from the wind. While we were there a seal and many beach turtles were sleeping on the beach. Volunteers did create a perimeter to protect the animals but you could around close to them to get pictures.The snorkeling was great here even very close to the shore. I was actually worried about stepping on sea urchins, that is how close they are. If you do make it here make sure to get a hot dog at Puka Dog, they were incredible!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach with turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is lovely like a lot of the beaches in Kauai, but with Poipu beach, you are more likely to get a beautiful sunny day. There were 5-6 turtles basking in the sun when we were there, and this made it extra special.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nature abounds
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Poipu Beach three times during our stay at Lihue.  Each time we were thrilled to see green sea turtles resting on the beach.  The best time to go to see the turtles in between 5:30-6:30pm/  Volunteers are there to answer any turtle questions you might have and they also ensure that the turtles are kept safe.  One of the afternoons we were there we also got to see a resting Hawaiian monk seal.  The water is shallow and calm because of a protective reef, that makes it perfect for children and relaxing sea bathers.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Everyone told us Poipou was beautiful, man were they right. Early morning drive from our condo and found parking around 10. Was about to snag a spot near the closest lifeguard tower. Made lunch and brought with us.  Beautiful scenery, water was warm and crystal clear. Sand was soft but hot in the sun. A packed beach on a Sunday. Even watched our a visiting seal basque in the sun all day. What an experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Mandatory stop
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One of the most beautiful beaches on Kauai!We went there early in the morning and I recommend it because there are fewer people.Suitable for both children and adults.We found two very large turtles... truly incredible!!!It is still possible to do a bit of snorkelling although as the water is shallow the coral reef has obviously been affected... what a shame!There is ample free parking which is unique as it has never happened to me in the USA!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunset at Poipu Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our favorite beach on south Kauai, hands down. We observed monk seals & talked to the volunteers. The sea turtles come ashore. We counted dozens. Just beautiful! Sunset our last night in Kauai was top notch at Poipu Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach park is great for snorkeling and to see the seals wash up on the shore. Can't beat the beautiful sunset view. *Would recommend water shoes due to the sharp rocks in shallow areas.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for novice snorkelers and kids
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach area has two things going in its favor:- the waters are really shallow - it's like knee or waist deep, so it's perfect for the kids. If you go closer to the rocks, the waters are so shallow that the toddlers can stand there. Yet, there are actually pretty big fish swimming around, so it's fine for beginner snorkeling. Plus, there are life guards. - the turtles come and rest for the night. They will literally swim up to the beach and sun themselves. There are docents who make sure that the turtles are unharmed while on the beach, this is great. But there are those out there who literally stick their underwater cameras with selfie sticks right in front of them, and some of them follow the turtle around to the point that the turtle could not get on the beach. It was frustrating to watch such people disturbing nature. This place is definitely a must for everyone, as long as they respect the space for the turtles and the seals (these animals have their designated safe zones on the beach, which interestingly seem to know).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Decent beach with free parking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach has restrooms and restaurants nearby with free parking. The sand and water are nice but bring your own shade (umbrella). As the island was created from volcanos there is lots of stone in the water so beach shoes are recommended. Snorkeling is pretty good right off the beach and we had turtles coming in to sun themselves right on our beach. Over 60 of them at night.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was outstanding. Really good snorkeling and swimming. I would recommend bringing water shoes as there are some rocks in water. Both days there was saw Turtles and Hawaii Monk Seals come ashore. This is our favorite beach in Kauai.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Sunset with Sea Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Seeing the Sea Turtles at Popiu Beach at Sunset is a Must!Every night a crowd gathers to see them coming ashore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Watch out for rocks
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach with lifeguard but lots of peopleCome with shoes to go in the water because there are lots of rocksWe were able to see a seal and turtles

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sea Turtles everywhere!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a beautiful walk down the beach. We saw 30+ turtles in the evening at the park. I recommend going about 30 minutes before sunrise to maximize turtle life.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach was super busy around sunset. I stopped by for dinner and to catch sunset. Amazing! I saw 10 sea turtles! Even though the beach was busy it was right out of a postcard!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice stop while exploring the south side of Kauai
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach with ample parking and restaurants nearby.  A lot of people were snorkeling and swimming.  We saw 2 monk seals and a green sea turtle resting on the beach. We were exploring the south side of the island and spent about 30 minutes here.  It would be a great place to spend several hours or more.  There are shade trees, a grassed area and pavilions.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good Day Beach, but Destructive to Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s a great place to gather. The bathrooms are usually clean and comfortable. There are almost always tables and pavilions available. Beach is great for snorkeling. I have to leave when the turtles arrive. I can’t see how the current crowd enforcement is adequate enough for the turtles to do whatever they need to do without disruption. My family likes the spectacle, but I find it unbearable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Such a great time!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a great time!  We visited this beach multiple times during our stay.  It just kind of had everything we needed.  It is a good spot for snorkeling, they have lifeguards on duty, there are restrooms and even showers.  We never had a very hard time finding a spot on the beach or in the parking lot (I'm sure other times of the year that may not be the case).   It's just a beautiful place and it worked out very well for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach for turtle watching, snorkeling and surfing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach with a shallow lagoon for snorkeling and a long strip of waves for surfing. There are camping tables, bathrooms and a restaurant with hot dogs and drinks. In the mornings a dozen large green turtles come out to sun themselves and rest.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Wonderful beach for swimming, surfing, & snorkeling. But the best part was seeing the turtles come up at dusk onto the beach. Amazing! There was also a monk seal taking a nap on the beach when we arrived. They do rope off the area to respect the seals and give space for the turtles. The sunset here was also beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach, maybe 20 mins off the main road, tree tunnel.There were 3 green sea turtles resting on the sand and one active it the water at the time. They’re about 2 ft long so pretty big.Lots of people in the water as it might be the only beach nearby. The beach is sheltered by some rocks so looked like a good place for kids.We didn’t go in as it was just a quick detour

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wildlife and amenities!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We wanted a beach with facilities. Here were toilets, showers, a beach but also grass to park on. Enough parking spaces. We also found shady spots under the palm trees. It's always a good idea to move with the sun haha.Be sure to bring water shoes. You get out of the water a little more charming. The sea was a bit restless for us, but you can walk to a bay. Also safer for children.When we were there, 50 meters from us were the turtles coming out of the water and 50 meters in the other direction the sea lions. Still very special. Sometimes you don't even notice that a turtle is swimming past you (if he/she comes from the sea) from the beach you just follow the herd of tourists. Fortunately, there are many volunteers who keep an eye on the animals and happily give some tourists a pat on the head. Wild animals remain. So this beach is definitely recommended. You can do some snorkeling but the sea can be a bit rougher.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach but not easy to just show up
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We ended up here after a brunch nearby and just wanted to stop in and see the beach.  It was a pretty area, but not really set up for a walk as it is smaller and fills in with people early.  The Puka Dog restaurant nearby is almost its own reason to come here and have a dog while looking out at the ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It's a beach - but not the best one!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed in both Poipu and Princeville during our stay and tried a number of beaches.  This beach is pretty, but seems VERY busy at all times.  There are better beaches on the south shore to go -- we loved Kiahuna Beach (much less busy, just as pretty or more than Poipu) and Salt Pond Beach Park (a 30 minute drive to the west, but very quiet and gorgeous).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went at sunset. Beautiful beach, fun to see the sea turtles & monk seals. Too many clueless people crowding to really let the wildlife who inhabit the area come up. Would be better if people had the sense to back up and let the monk seals & turtles have the space they need & deserve.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: It was a great beach...until some older ladies adorned it with orange cones
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We used to love this beach! A few years ago, when we lingered past the sunset, we got to watch a caravan of green turtles come ashore one by one to rest. After the amazing opportunity to enjoy watching these beautiful creatures, we walked away grateful and satisfied. Fast forward to this year, what a difference! As if the large crowd wasn't bad enough, some "turtle saviors" put ugly orange cones, signs with lights (while telling spectators not to use theit lights) around turtles that were coming onto the beach to rest. A gray-haired neurotic lady ran between the cones, repositioning them and gathering a huge crowd around "teaching" everyone how not to behave. Lady, for starters, why don't you share with the crowd how many green sea turtle die from a 5 year old looking at it in amazement? The ugly orange cones, endless signs and crazy lights don't protect them from overdevelopment of the shoreline or the fishermen nets they get tangled in. You are truly ruining a beautiful beach to feed your overinflated ego. Stop caging the turtles and turning their resting sites into a zoo display! What a shame...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sensational snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a great time snorkeling. We were able to see many different types of tropical fish in waist high water. Monk seal was resting on the sand nearby.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Favorite beach to snorkel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Snorkeling on this beach is one of the best. Little rocky getting in but worth it. Usually see turtles resting on the sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but rocky
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Super rockyIt's looks beautiful with an amazing sandbar so we took the time to come back to swim and found its all rocks except for the little pool to the left. Be careful!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkeling and surfing beach with wildlife!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A very nice beach here that has a lot to offer for families. The area closer to the shore is not heavy with current due to the protective barrier, making it ideal for snorkeling. There was a good variety of fish to see and very close to the shore. Lots of rocky areas, so water shoes would be advisable. Great surfing available to the left and right of the snorkeling area. Beach was very crowded and it’s a smaller beach, so it feels more crowded than it is. We saw sea turtles on the shore while there! Great place to visit in the south shore!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Would stay away from turtles and monk seals
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful small beach. There is an area walled off with lava rock for younger kids. Sometimes in the mornings at low tide it is less than 12 inches deep with minimal waves like a wading pool. Near the end of the rock wall the current gets much stronger with floor covered in lava rock but lots of fish for snorkelers. Would recommend kids always wear water shoes because there are random sharp rocks still in the sandy area. There is a play structure, grassy area, Puka Dog hot dogs and shaved ice within walking distance. Sunsets are beautiful.One issue with this place though- it is now overrun by people. The poor turtles that come up to the beach to rest and sleep at sunset have a bunch of tourists who surround them taking video and selfies with them. They have a very small fraction of the beach set up with cones but still people routinely ignore and walk right up to them. Sad to see such disrespect.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sea turtles at the beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very small beach.  We saw sea turtles 🐢  so that was cool.  They were just resting on the beach. The water had rocks not best place to swim. Imo

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach where you can see turtles swimming during the day and they go to shore at night
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Fun beach, we saw lots of turtles Snorkeling is goodThe only thing is, rocks at the bottom could be uncomfortable, I would suggest water shoes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a great time and this is a nice beach with parking, not much on Kauai offers parking. The floor has plenty of rocks so having shoes or flippers will be important. The sea turtles were on the beach and a fun feature.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It’s easy to understand why this beautiful beach is popular with families. It’s clean and safe (with life guards alertly watching over water activities). There’s a grassy area for sunbathers. Soft sand and gentle waves beckoned. Clear water made for great snorkeling: our grandkids loved seeing colorful fishes near the corals. We watched a steady stream of arriving & departing visitors parading by with surf boards, boogie boards, beach chairs, umbrellas, and coolers. Bathrooms were clean. Parking lot was not full yet when we arrived around 11am. Judging from the turnovers, finding a vacant spot in the lot or on the beach shouldn’t be an issue. It got hotter and windy in the afternoon. There’s a Marriott Vacation Beach Club on the right flank within walkable distance for nice tropical refreshments to cool off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: WOW
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Well, my wife's first time snorkeling.  Bay was a little choppy, and small rip tides, but she was a trooper. Busy place but very nice. Try to check conditions before going, but, go, it'll be worth it.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Monk seals
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Strong current in summer but still beautiful with monk seals laying on the beach. Always see a turtle or two here. Easy nearby parking and facilities.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Seal you tomorrow
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A nice beach in Poipu with bathrooms and ample parking that's close to restaurants resorts and shops. The other highlight are the seals that frequent the beach (no touching!). The cons are that the beach area is kind of small especially with all the people and the sand quality is average and there's not much shade so bring an umbrella.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rough waves! Use caution (younger families and older folks or beginners)
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach. But it depends on what you are there for.   I guess I am giving it a poorer rating because my experience was negative and it needs to be explained that this beach is NOT, in my opinion, for the very young or elderly. The water was very rough while we were there and it was impossible - and even dangerous - for me to navigate in the water to snorkel or swim because I have arthritis in my knees. I have snorkeled a bit and am comfortable in the water, but in this circumstance, I was not able to gain footing and stay on my feet long enough to get over the swath of coral reef to actually snorkel. I am not blaming the beach but it is not good to have expectations that this beach is good for everyone, especially beginner snorkelers. I got cut all over my hands and legs trying to get back to shore. It didn’t help that I felt a thousand eyes on me. 🙄 Perhaps there are times when the waves are milder. I don’t know! First time here. Just be aware that it may not be suitable for you or your family. It is not a mild, Florida beach where you can sit back in a lawn chair and watch your toddlers play in the waves. Or where your low mobility elderly parents can go in for a dip.On the positive side, it is so picturesque and the sand is lovely, as is the beauty of the crashing waves. Once I recovered from my attempt to snorkel, I enjoyed sitting on the sand and people and wave watching.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Turtles! There were turtles here every time we came during our vacation and often monk seals too. At night, even more turtles come to the shore to lounge. It's a popular beach with a lot of people so volunteers keep the turtles safe. Many people snorkel here as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Monk seal
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was there around noon. I didn't see any sea turtles, but I saw one big monk seal was sleeping on the beach.A lot of people were at the beach, even though the wave was high, some people were swimming, snorkeling and surfing. There were two life guards on site.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful! A must in Kauai
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful!!! Our favorite beach in all of kauai; the water is just stunning. Laid back and plenty of parking

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Early morning or evening snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our favorite place to snorkel as beginners. Saw sea turtles, variety of fish, water was sometimes rough, but good protected areas to snorkel. Follow lifeguards' instructions

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach for snorkeling, Don3t miss early mornings and sunset!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked to Poipu beach every morning after watching the sunrise at Shipwreck beach the 1st week of April. We sat on the rocks and watched turtles swimming and whale spouts in the distance. We came back around 5pm every night when the day-time crowds diminished to snorkel and watch the sunset. There is nothing like snorkeling while the turtles swim to shore for the night, then enjoying a puka dog while watching the sun sink into the ocean!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Large open space with green grass, shade available. A lot of people and kids. Food available nearby. Small protected area for kids.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Monk Seal and turtle sightings here!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach, but not for swimming. There were warning signs everywhere and no lifeguards, This was a great place to see Monk Seals, and sea turtles as they beach themselves just before sunset. There were lots of turtle conservationists who kept the people 10 feet away and answered all our questions about these creatures. The sunset was beautiful here too. Definitely worth visiting even though we didn't go in the water.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach.  There were several tourists but we never felt it was overcrowded.  The waves were on the small side which made it nice for swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: SNORKEL, TURTLES AND SEALS!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Must see beach! I saw tons of turtle on the sand and seals! You can snorkeling in this area but BRING WATER SHOES and your snorkel gear. You can also rent equipment across the street from beach. Give yourself some time here!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunset, turtles and whales
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove here to watch the sunset our last night and were treated with sea turtles coming ashore and whales splashing around on the horizon.  Also stopped at Puka dog across the street for a light snack before supper.  There were people snorkeling in the water, but since it was sunset and we weren't there for that, we did not get in.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Sunset and Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is a great place for snorkeling, etc. Also my wife and I like to go there every time we’re in Kauai to enjoy the sunsets, and this time we went just in time to watch the sea turtles come up onto the beach for the night. The area was scattered with people and all were having a very nice experience. Peaceful and beautiful time was had by all.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to see turtles and seals
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent a pleasant day at Poipu Beach Park where we saw several large turtles on the beach and a monk seal sleeping in the sand.  It's a nice place to relax and enjoy the sunshine and walk along the beach.  There were public restrooms but they were pretty gross and the showers outside did not work so it wasn't possible to wash off the sand.  We were there on a Sunday and it was crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enjoyable beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed a Sunday afternoon at Poipu Beach. Definitely a busier spot, but we were still able to find a good spot to camp out on the beach and enjoy the water. Saw some beautiful fish while snorkeling and lots of tortoises on the beach. Would definitely recommend hitting up the nearby Puka Dog for lunch or dinner that you can take back to the beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy but beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pretty beach, good for snorkelling with a view of seals and turtles that come up on the shore! Some areas are good for swimming and protected from large waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sea turtles basking on the beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: With rain in the northern part of Kauai, we were told it was drier in the south so we made our way to Poipu Beach. Nice quiet area and it was fascinating to see at least 10 sea turtles on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach for kids and snorkelers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I love Poipu Beach. It's a nice big beach with trees and picnic areas. The far left of the beach is protected by big rocks and is shallow for kids to swim and play. The right side of the beach is rocky so water shoes are recommended, but is great for snorkeling with many pretty colored fish.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AS GOOD AS IT GETS
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Want to make your friends jealous with views from the perfect Hawaiian beach?  Look no further than Poipu.  Great, protected swimming area (lifeguards on guard to make sure knuckleheads don't go out too far and get into trouble) with lots of fish for snorkeling.  Saw lots of turtles hauled out and even a monk seal.  PLEASE be mindful of the signs and barriers and don't get too close.  So thankful the volunteers were there to keep the knuckleheads away from these beautiful and majestic animals!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always turtles and monk seals.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I don't think much of Poipu for swimming, as it is a bit small. But whenever I was there I saw turtles, seals, or both.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: turtles and seals and gorgeous sunset!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: beautiful beach. sunset time turtles come in to sleep here, and seals too! good parking across from the beach that is usually full but we got lucky daily. too crowded in February's rainy season, can't imagine how many humans flock here in their high season! Sat here reading my book under a tree watching people and the ocean.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great spot for all kinds of beach experiences
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I spent almost an entire day here: sunbathing on the sand, watching giant turtles crawl in and out of the surf, poking into tide pools, and snorkeling a bit in the “kiddie pool” area. There are plenty of tables and trees for folks who’d prefer a little less sun and heat, and the shops nearby offer tasty treats. The shuttle drops you off just a short (~8 min) walk from the beach and is much easier than parking.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice day for sunning like a monk seal
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice but busy beach. Turtles and monk seals abound. Don’t forget to admire from afar. And if near the seals be ready for them to switch positions. Wear good water shoes, rock abounds

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is a relatively small and crowded beach on the south coast of Kauai.  There are two parts to the beach and you can easily walk to the beaches on either side of it.  There are lifeguards during the day.  In the evening many Hawaiian Green Turtles come to the east end of the beach to rest for the night.  We saw upwards of 40 turtles.  Hawaiian Monk Seals also sometimes spend the day sleeping and sunning on the beach.  Snorkeling was decent though limited.  The lifeguards limited where we could snorkel due to water currents and high waves during our visit.  The water was shallow which made for some challenges.  There were actually a surprising number and variety of fish despite all of the people thrashing around in the water.  Portions of the beach have rocks which make entry more difficult, but there are sandy areas as well.  Stay to the left for the best snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for snorkeling and seeing a variety of marine life
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was my favorite beach of the ones we visited in Kauai. We went snorkeling and I was amazed at the clarity of the water and the variety of marine life so close to shore. Definitely wear water shoes - I cut my foot coming back to the beach from the water on a rock. There were many people boogie boarding and it seemed like they enjoyed themselves as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: turtles right on the sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: going here again, the best resort on this stretch is KoaKea resort(check it out), the beach is amazing for swimming and snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Go “sea” the turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Popped in half hour before sunset- lucky to get a parking spot but with patience more we’re to be had as families were leaving too. We went to see the sea turtles, 42 in total- - saw a seal as well. Beautiful spot to catch a sunset as well or walk the beach. Laid back crowd. Glad we drove 40 min for the experience.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach for snorkeling & turtle watching
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed this beach to see the turtles & seals and the one further down by the Beach House resturant where we rented snorkels, chairs and umbrellas for 24 hours. It was rocky & we needed water shoes, but we saw lots of fish.  Free parking and clean restrooms. Places to eat close by.  A wonderful beach to put your feet in the sand. We all said next time we'd like to stay close to here & be able to walk down everyday.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach on south shore
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach, clean, busy.Lots of attractions - sea lions and turtles up on shore resting/sleeping.Lots of parking Loved it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Come a half hour before sunset to see turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poʻipū Beach is located directly opposite of Puka's Hotdogs. We used the parking lot next door and then walked across to see the sea turtles before purchasing food from this place. Starting at around a half hour before sunset,  leatherback and green sea turtles, known in Hawaiian as "honu" swim to the shores to rest at night on Poʻipū Beach.Flashlights, flash photography and even bright street lights are not allowed because sea birds and turtles get confused thinking that they're going towards the sea where the moonlight is, and instead go inland and get hit by cars or attacked by dogs.There is a turtle group that keeps watch over the turtles from sundown until sun up in shifts to protect the turtles from poachers and evil people who would try to harm these magnificent creatures. Native Hawaiians are doing God's work when it comes to animal stewardship.Visited: January 2023

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome Beach with many unexpected sights...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We saw Turtles sunning on the beach and a Hawaiian Monk Seal. All endangered. Great sunsets!! One of the most beautiful beaches in the world!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach to relax at all day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was the fourth beach that we visited during our trip and it was one of our favorites. The photos we took here were really good. The parking was a little crowded but other than that it was excellent

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool Beach Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We walked down to the beach at the park each morning - beautiful spot.  Turtles on the beach each morning - cool to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Gorgeous beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not only is it one of the best spots on the island to watch Hawaii's spectacular sunsets, but it's a prime spot for swimming thanks to a coral reef. As it's so popular, it was hard to find a spot in the parking lot, come early if possible. You can easily rent boogie boards, surfboards, snorkeling gear, umbrella and more as there are plenty of concessions nearby.Good sanitary facilities with changing rooms, picnic areas with benches and barbecues. There are outdoor showers with cold water and finally a lifeguard on duty.It is common to see endangered Hawaiian Monk Seals lounging peacefully on the beach or taking a nap. They are highly respected beauties, volunteers set up and moved a cordon around the seal areas as they moved, to hold people back. Remember that harassing or harming a Hawaiian Monk Seal is a felony. Great place to snorkel, beautiful scenery and bodyboarders are awesome to watch. In summary, soft sand, great atmosphere, beautiful views. It really is a must-visit beach during your stay in Kauai. Enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful view but busy
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great pier but busy location. We swung by mid-day on Monday during the holidays and the place was packed. There is a parking lot across the street but it fills up quickly, we followed the crowd and parallel parked on the side of a road. Then we walked down the pier and got some great photos.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We came here because supposedly it is the safest for swimming during the winter. There is a lifeguard. It is too crowded. Even on Christmas Eve it was hard to find parking and hard to find a place to put our chairs that was not on top of others. Nasty chickens running all over the place. There were signs warning of man of war jellyfish. Two seals in a corded off area taking a nap. The swimming and snorkeling was not great as there are nothing but sad dead reefs and just a few colorful fish.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Green Hawaiian Sea Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped by the beach on two different days at sunset. Each time, we got to see 30-40 Green Sea Turtles come ashore to sleep for the night. Such a fantastic and amazing display of nature. It gets pretty crowded right before sunset, but the crowd thins out by last light. There are volunteers in the area to make sure people aren't using flash photography and are respectful of the turtles by keeping marking off an area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Poipu Beach- Pleasant
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Free parking directly across the street was convenient. Watching the many turtles crawl ashore to sunbathe was a delightful show.  We visited on a Saturday yet it was still peaceful.  No loud music.  Lots of families.  Worth a visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkeling, Hawaiian Monk Seals and Giant Sea Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The snorkeling and surfing were great but we also enjoyed viewing the wildlife on shore.  Community volunteers were on duty each day and evening to create safety zones for the beached seals and turtles.  They were still easily visible.  One evening we counted more than 20 turtles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but busy go to beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu beach was beautiful but VERY busy it is the go-to beach.  The sea turtles and the sea lions come up on shore and you can snorkel with them too - just keep your distance.  the day we were here it was very hot and very worth the beach day.  We brought our snorkel gear and checked out all the underwater scenery.  definately recommend!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Family Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is spacious, friendly and a superb place to cool off.  The water in the bay only goes to your knees...if that far. You'll have to sit down to get wet which is what most visitors do.  They just sit in the water and cool off.  It's a great place for younger kids to play and be safe.If you want to snorkel, you can snorkel in the shallow area.  Just go out to the lava rocks and put your face in the water.  You will be many fish around the rocks.  If you want more adventure, venture into the deeper water to the right and join the other snorkelers.  Best thing about this beach...the green sea turtles sunbathing on the shore.  They come and go as they please and everyone makes room for them as they do.  So much fun to watch.  Waiting for them to move though is like watching pain dry.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles, Turtles, Turtles!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was by far the best beach we went to for snorkeling.  We saw 6 turtles on the beach as well as a seal!  They were all so cute!!  There were also tons of fish iin the calm waters right off of shore!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pleasant Beach Adventure
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Enjoyable beach nearby our condo. It is very popular and had gentle waves. There is plenty of snorkeling at this beach. Also a chance to see sea turtles.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sea turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We enjoyed coming to Poipu Beach at dusk to see the sea turtles that make their way onto the beach.  Snorkeling was also good here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for snorkeling and sea life
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Protected cove beach sets up amazing for snorkeling. Plenty of room throughout the water and the beach. When we arrived both seals and sea turtles were resting on the beach. Best snorkel spot is just to the right of the center sand bar.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Poipu beach was the best for snorkeling!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Poipu after our ATV tour in Koloa.  There was plenty of parking and the beach access was easy.  This beach is great for snorkeling.  This beach was definitely child friendly.  We didn't get a chance to see turtles but we heard from others that turtles line up on the shore between6:30-8:00 A.M. every morning.  This beach was beautiful with clear waters and lots of colorful fish to see.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Many people but for a good reason
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach park is a very popular place so expect many people but for many reasons: part of the crescent white beach has not waves and is ideal for kids, part of it offers great snorkling with lots of colorful fish, some corals and seals and turtles occasionallly resting on the small sand bank just off the beach, excellent waves and surf for bodysurfing in a different section of the beach. You do not feel that you are surrounded by mass tourism even when the big hotels surround the beach, as these are built in low and appealing architechture. Good parking and rinsing facilities also. So do not miss Poipu where the sun almost always shines.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Please respect the Turtles people!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Respect the Turtles people ! Covid left the beach empty. Now turtles come each night to rest. They feel safe. Beautiful beach but respect , keep your distance .Some kids tried to sit on turtle's. Kids swim near the turtles .Poor volunteers do their best job. People shine  lights at them after being asked “ not to”.I’m so afraid this beautiful experience will end.It’s a great beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Came to see the sunset...stayed for the turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a great beach!  We didn't get to go snorkeling because we arrived just barely before sunset, but the drive was worth it when we saw the sunset and the turtles beaching themselves.  It got dark very quickly, so if you don't arrive early enough you'll not be able to see them very well.  We heard there would also be seals down the beach a ways, but we never saw any when we walked down.  Nonetheless, the turtles were worth it - there was probably 30+ that evening and the docent said that the average is anywhere between 30-70!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful sandy beach with great access
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Family friendly beach with pretty good access. Parking lot is across the street but still less than 100 yards to the nice sandy beach. Lots of grassy areas to put your chairs or blankets to relax in the sun. Beach drops off pretty quickly so be careful with small children.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun for the whole family
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of fish 🐠 for snorkeling. Kiddie area for the little guys. We had two monk seals come into the beach area and play for hours! So much fun to watch them- they were friendly and hammed it up for the tourists!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Saw turtles here!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was an amazing beach where the turtles are just chilling! Well worth seeing and getting up early in the morning to enjoy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not the best beach in Poipu.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach nearest the park has a lot of rocks, so is difficult to get in & out.  The beach to the right is less rocky, but had too much swell to enjoy swimming.  Over-rated.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtle Town
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Calm surf, good snorkeling, nice sunset. This is THE place to see turtles after sunset and early AM ( 6 am). Showers and picnic tables too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you want to snorkel, this is the place.  Easy access and snorkeling right off the beach.  Nice place to take kids as the large swim area is relatively calm.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing Snokeling/Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: So many fish to see snorkeling. We even saw a huge sea turtle. Nice beach, plenty of parking and room available for people to spread out. Nice sand bar blocking a lot of stronger currents/waves for new snorkelers. Plenty of shallow areas for younger kids as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach all around.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach! It has bathrooms, lifeguards, and is right across the street from shopping/food/shave ice. The 4 year old could play in the sand & calm water, while the rest of us snorkeled. It was my first time snorkeling so I can't compare it to anywhere else, but a sea turtle swam right in front of me, and there were so many fish and sea urchins to look at it. And a huge highlight - watching the sea turtle that was still on the beach slowly walk/swim away when he was ready! We returned that night for shave ice and to watch the turtles come back. Felt like a true Hawaiian experience for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Better for snorkeling than swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very rocky bottom which is great for snorkeling but not as great for swimming.  Easy to bang your feet and ankles and cut them.  But great for snorkeling.  A seal rolled up and situated himself on the beach while we were there and behaved very much as though the rest of the world ought to accommodate his 20 feet distance rule.  And the rest of the world did indeed accommodate.  He chilled for long enough that when we went back in the water he was still there relaxing on the beach.  Beautiful moment.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach for swimming snorkeling and turtles
