reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu is beautiful. It’s a very calm protected beach where everyone can get in the water. Snorkeling is good too. It can get a little crowded at times compared to other beaches in Hawaii. Worth the visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Snorkel here about the best place this time of yr. good place to swim for all ages but might want water shoes. Great views and stay for sunset. Monk seal was sleeping on the beach while we were there. Also every other Sun afternoon a group of locals get together and play ukeleles. Very informal very nice group. Im not sure they want publicity though. They have bathroom, lifeguard and restaurant/shop across the street.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing beach for families
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach with protected sandy area for toddlers, plus good snorkelling.  Frequently turtles or seals resting on the beach too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach on Kauai's South Shore
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is a very nice, white sand beach where you can set up your sand chair and relax the hours away. Or you can hop on your boogie board or surf board or grab a sandwich at the local deli across the street or people watch.The beach has a life guard, restrooms and showers. There is a grassy area behind the beach where you can have a picnic, play frisbee or hang out.Parking is across the street with some spots on the street. Beware: it does get a little crowded, especially the weekend. Bring chairs, beach umbrella, your sunglasses and plenty of suntan lotion!If you have snorkel gear, you might bring that, too, although I did not see many people snorkeling on the several occasions I was there.Great sunsets, too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lifeguard on duty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the areas there is a lifeguard. The beach area is both sand or grass. There are several covered areas to picnic or just get out of the sun. The grassy area is full of tiny pine cones from the trees, so wear something on your feet.  While we were there a large green sea turtle came upon the beach.  It was beautiful  to see, but so  sad that so many people did not respect the large animal and did not give it room. The guards were told, but nothing done.  They needs some  conservationist on duty to educate the public.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots of fish!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Shallow and clear beach with lots of fish and fish species. Swam monk seals who had just been sleeping on beach and then entered the water. Saw a moray eel resident who lives on one the shelves about 60 feet out. Not really a swimming beach per se due to corals and shallowness but lots of young kid with parents loved it. If you want to go into deeper water there are numerous other beaches just north or south at 5 minute drives. We came back twice to Poipu due to ease of snorkeling. Love it !!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful family beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for family fun. Fun restaurant across the street. Plenty of room so don’t feel crowded. Can easily walk to it if staying close by the area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Not so great
reviewsWithKeywords.text: First, Whoever claims this is good Snorkeling hasn’t been lately (or at all). It’s cloudy visibility, (and we were there on a dry sunny week), totally overcrowded (and this was off season!), topography was sparse or just dead, and although we saw a few schools of fish through the churned up water, they seemed as though people were feeding them (so absolutely WRONG). Lifeguards are yelling into bullhorns every few minutes at unsafe surfers and swimmers without fins, so don’t count on any peaceful garden- island moments at this spot. Go to the north for peace and fewer crowds.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach. It sits in front of Kiahuna Plantation Resort and next to the Sheraton Hotel.  There are no lifeguards here.  There is a small public parking area in front of the beach.  Great waves and a few surfers.  Not too crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice place to snorkel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice, protected, place to snorkel or swim.  The is a lot of parking and a lot of beach, but this place gets really busy!  We saw a Hawaiian Monk Seal basking on the shore as well as two large sea turtles.  The are a fair amount of fish swimming around.   To the left when facing the ocean is the calmest water.  Just at the edge where the sand ends and the rocks begin the are hundreds of different fish.  There are outdoor showers and restrooms here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: AMAZING Snorkeling & Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed next to this beach and snorkeled every day seeing amazing variety of fish and we saw several turtles dock this beach to lay out. It was incredible. There is also a great surf break to the right of the beach in front of the Marriott. You can enjoy all the water activities at this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach with lifeguards and great snorkeling.  Also much wildlife.  You will see sea turtles and monk seals as well as a lot of fish!  Lively beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunset Paradise
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is probably one of the most beautiful, peaceful, isolated beaches you will ever visit. My first morning consisted of three seals asleep on a sandbar and a mama sea turtle asleep on the beach.  Great waves with lots of beginning surfers,  and lots of colorful fish to view just a few feet off the shore.   The sunsets combined with the roaring waves made this place Paradise.  Can't wait to go back.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach for families and couples.  Swimming areas with lifeguards and a small "island" to swim to about 20 yards from shore.  There are beach areas and rocky areas if you want to swim or just watch the waves crash against the rocks.  And right across the street is Brennecke's Beach Broiler for food and drinks.  Poipu beach is one of my wife's favorite places to be.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Busy But Worth It. Good Snorkelling!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very busy beach, but surprisingly, you won't mind the crowds. It's a wonderfully happy, sunny spot with a protected area for swimming and snorkelling. The abundance of tropical fish you can see are greater in number than at many other snorkelling sports on the islands. And BONUS- there's a deli across the park where you can pick order sandwiches to go and beer for your cooler! There are often turtles and mom seals resting on the sand. You need keep your distance from these protected animals. Take a sand umbrella for some shade.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely park/beach to spend a few hours at.  There is a beach and lawn area with plenty of picnic tables in the shade.  Lifeguard stand and protected cove area are good for children to swim.  I saw turtles swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great snorkeling and swimming
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great place to swim and snorkel on Kauai.  Sea turtles and monk seals are frequent visitors to this area including lounging on the beach while you swim.   Amazing variety of tropical fish species makes this an excellent place to snorkel and view marine wildlife.  Hundreds of tropical fish are present every time we swim here. Beach House happy hour is right down the road.   Highly recommended.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Favorite beach in Kauai
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach has it all...beautiful sandy beach; safe for kids and timid swimmers; lifeguards; great snorkeling; grassy area; picnic areas; parking; restrooms and frequent ocean visitors-monk seals and turtles!  It's a lovely spot for sunrise and sunset.We miss the tombolo-a sandy strip of land that connected from the beach to a little "island".  It's made snorkeling on the right side almost obsolete due to rip currents, rough conditions.  However, there is still great snorkeling to the left.Hope the tombolo comes back!Poipu beach is very clean and family friendly. I suggest getting there early as it has become quite busy since the north shore beaches are closed (north of Hanalei)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Small but family friendly
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a small beach on the south side that seemed very safe fro families with smaller kids.  It is also the one place on this part of the island where snorkeling seems to be done (although I am not sure what people can see there).

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful public beach - a must if you're on Kauai
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to Poipu Beach Park after a happy hour meal to walk the beach, take in the sights, & unwind. It is the perfect spot for that - & for playing in the ocean, snorkeling (there's a sheltered cove,) eating a picnic/snack, & people watching. As the sun set, several sea turtles even came up on the beach to hang out with us. Very cool - If you're on Kauai, this beach park is a MUST.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Poipu Beach while staying at the grand Hyatt resort because we couldn’t swim in the ocean at the hotel due to high waves. This popular beach was very clean and very swim friendly. The crystal clear water was awesome to snorkel and see colorful fish. The only downfall was the limited parking. You should get there early for good close parking located directly across the street. I highly recommend it

reviewsWithKeywords.title: swim super but Monk Seals is the most interesting
reviewsWithKeywords.text: yes of course it is nice for swimming but the most interesting is that there are nearly every Monk Seals coming on the sand for a rest and they lay there for hours, you can get very close to them(around 5-10 yards) As soon as they arrive people make  a kind of fence in order to protect and avoid that tourist get to close ( it is absolutley forbidden to get close and touch) we have seen them every day.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach on the south shore
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent a really nice beach day here. It was a very nice area with bathrooms and parking available. We had a great time snorkeling and saw lots of pretty fish in very clear waters. Definitely need to bring water shoes as many in our group left with cut up feet from the rocks and coral on the bottom of the water. Not a great place to take a beach walk or really play in the water due to the rocky bottom, but still a great place to be!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: our favorite beach in Poipu
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gentle waves in an ideal ocean temperature!  Great views of the sunsets nightly!  Not crowded; easy access to parking

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Enjoy the Sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our end of day destination. Great sunsets. Snorkelling and just enjoying the relaxation. Park for kids and restaurants and bars aling the strip. Lifeguards. Surfers like sunset surfing.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: sunsets
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Gorgeous sunsets every single night we were there, safe swimming and great snorkeling. Water shoes are recommended, rocks cut through your feet

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great snorkeling beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is great for snorkeling.  There is an abundance of picnic tables, changing area and places to snack and eat across the street.  I saw a multitude of very colorful fish and on the sand bar was a sea turtle and sea lion!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Easy, nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a popular spot and for good reason. Easy in and out of the water, snorkeling is often good, turtles may be hanging out, and there are shady areas on the beach so you can get out of the sun. All the good things one likes in a beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach southern Kauai
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Free and easy parking. A 5 minute walk gets you to this beautiful beach. Swimming, snorkeling, sun bathing etc etc. Ample of space to find yourself a great spot. The ocean is pretty flat here so excellent for novice snorkelers. Brenneckes, is a 5 minute walk a great place to eat and drink with below a snack bar to get an ice cream, some chips or a drink. Changes are high to see a turtle moving onto the beach. With a lifeguard on duty you will be quite safe here. Enjoy, highly recommended.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Across fro Brennekes -- Monk seals and turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is our go to beach on Kauai. Lifeguards, nice grassy park, soft sand beach, toilets, lots of free parking, across from Brennekes ( a fave for dinner but also has snacks, rentals, snow cones, etc. The water is very nice -- not good for body surfing but some soft waves and a very protected area for the small kiddies off to the left. But Reef Walkers are a requirement for us -- the bottom is rocky. But the local Whalers Markets or ABC stores sell the reef walkers for about $10 a pair. Good snorkeling on the left side of the tombolo (the small island). Lots of fish. And there always seem to be 2 or 3 monk seals on the beach for a rest and usually a turtle, too. But stay back at least 15 feet or be prepared to pay a very stiff fine!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: First Hawaiian snorkel
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very clean beach and restrooms.  Plenty of showers outside and near sidewalk of grass not into more sand.  The lifegaurds were on the ball to anounce to people about cautions! But hard to understand the PA system.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Rough waves for snorkeling but best turtle viewing spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to Poipu Beach at 7 am - best time for calmer waves - but still very rough for snorkeling but best time to see giant sea turtles and monk seals which are going extinct - the sea turtles rest on this beach at night and return to the ocean in the morning - so great to see them early morning before they return - we also went about 8pm - saw 6 sea turtles but can’t use light - bad for the turtles - very hard to see them then - better to go early morning!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great beach for swimming, snorkeling and for children. It has a protected area that's like an ocean swimming pool. Has life guards too. Places to rent snorkeling gear, to eat, benches and tables that are covered and bathrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family friendly and absolutely beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a really nice place to take your family and snorkel in a protected area.  If you approach the water on the left side, the bottom is soft and sandy without rocks.  The snorkeling if good but not great visibility.  I saw lots of small fish, a sea turtle and there were 3 monk seals sleeping in the afternoon sun right on the beach!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with 3 seals.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great sand on this beach and there were 3 seals plopped on the beach where they cordoned off the area where they were to keep nosies away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best overall beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was our favorite beach because of it’s overall appeal to all ages: kids’ pool, snorkeling, boogie board, and seeing monks/turtles daily. I will go back here!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beach park for all ages. There is a wall to break the waves and allow for a small swimming cove for families and snorkelers. The snorkeling was fantastic.  Many different fish and lots of them. Picnic tables there. Showers and restrooms available.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Hardly any parking
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach is pretty decent. The sandbar doesn’t go very far out and the beach is a little small. Good luck finding parking unless you belong to the Sheraton hotel.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very pretty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a very pretty beach but we end up here every time the weather is bad and it's too murky to snorkel with too big of waves to enjoy the beach. We were able to see Munk seals and turtles and of course a glorious sunset.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fun time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is one of the most popular beaches on Kauai. For this reason it can be crowded by Kauai standards but nothing like you can find on Oahu or Maui. It is a beautiful beach and some decent snorkeling as well. We saw lots of fish not far from shore. We also saw a very endangered Hawaiian monk seal on the rocks there. It was great morning there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good snorkeling here and something for everyone with the protected “kiddy pool” area to the left (easy snorkeling entry from there). Common place to spot turtles or seals resting on the beach. The parking lot can fill up fast.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice safe beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is a safe beach for wading and snorkeling. There is lots of sea life at Poipu Beach and near by beaches. There are bathrooms.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Had a good time swimming and snorkeling. Pretty good snorkeling right off the beach. Surf shop With chair and equipment rental on site. Saw turtles, seals, tons of fish and of course the requisite chickens.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Not an easy place to swim but you can at least get in the water to swim, surf, snorkel or SUP. Great sunset views. Easy walking access to shops and restaurants.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The Poipu Beach Park was just a short walk from our timeshare. Every morning a beautiful sunrise and every evening a gorgeous sunset! The ocean is warm, clear and clean!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Favorite Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is a great option! This side of the island has the best weather. There are a couple of different spots on the beach depending on what you want to do (a calm area in the water to relax in, surfing, and an area with a bit more waves to ride). The beach and sand itself is nice too and there are grassy areas, playgrounds and sitting areas too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Honu and monk seals and beauty
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Beautiful beach on the south side of Kauai, where lots of sea turtles (honu) and mink seals hang out on the sand. Beautiful views, relatively clean, and gorgeous sunrises and sunsets. It gets crowded during the day, but coming out in time to see the turtles is usually pretty low key (gotta get out before the sunrise to see them, usually). We even found a whole big group of 7 turtles there in the evening (around 9 PM) sleeping on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sea turtles and amazing snorkeling!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We had an amazing experience at Poipu Beach! My husband said it’s like being in Finding Nemo, haha. So many amazing tropical fish and we even snorkeled next to a sea turtle! The lifeguards were awesome. They were friendly and super knowledgeable. The lifeguard I asked about the safest area for snorkeling knew right away what to tell us. He also gave helpful info on the trends of the tide/currents. My favorite part was seeing the sea turtles come to the beach after sunset!!! They are amazing. We had to leave for our flight, but an hour after sunset there were 8 I think.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Day at the Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a small beach but fairly well protected and has lifeguards.  The day we visited was a bit windy and was a bit tricky for snorkeling or boogie boarding.  However, there were good facilities and good parking.  It seemed like there were a good many locals as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Kids' Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you have little ones, this is your destination!  We have had some sweet family vacations here.  Also, Anini Beach on the north shore is perfect for families, too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is on the dry side of the island. We would walk along the road to get to the beach and from the road you could see the sea turtles it is a great snorkeling Beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Went for a swim
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stopped here for a swim the other day. The beach was crowded but we did find room for the 2 of us. They have a decent bathroom and change room onsite.We had been here before and we both thought there was more sand. You can only take a couple of steps out into the water and you run into lava rocks everywhere.We wished we would have brought our aqua socks with us : ( Still a nice pleasant swimable beach area.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A quick visit
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Just popped in for a quick visit to see if we could see a monk seal Luckily we were rewarded with one sunning himself out on the sand bar. Lovely beach and worth another visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach, Nice Water, Lots of Rocks and Coral
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu Beach is a great beach. Sand is beautiful, water is very clear. I snorkeled at this beach - lots of fish in the water. Water was a little rough but very manageable. Lots of fun!! Only reason I didn't go EXCELLENT on my review - once in the water, it is not sand based. There are way too many rocks and coral once you get in the water. I cut up my feet pretty bad. I wound up buying water shoes, but the damage to my feet was already done. Be warned!! Otherwise - all very good!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Family Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu was one of the beaches we wanted to go to to snorkel being very novice snorkelers.  The beach is nice and sandy but in the water the bottom is variable, with lava, coral and sand. Where we were the area was protected somewhat. The area has a lifeguard who had to come out of his little booth to tell us that we should move away from the area we were contemplating.  I guess we had greenhorns written all over us!  If unsure of the water, you should ask a lifeguard. Once in the water we did see lots of colorful fish tho the water was not as clear as I had hoped.  Maybe because of the recent hurricane activity?The park has restrooms with changing areas, picnic areas and children play areas - very family friendly and good for beginning snorkelers from Ohio!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: The best spt for sunset
reviewsWithKeywords.text: East acces parking depends on the day some tome you can park at the side of the road for short time and use the boat ramp parking for short timeVery family oriented beach sunset is amazing

reviewsWithKeywords.title: My favorite beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is an ideal park for families with young children. The water is relatively calm and bottom is sandy In places! You can see fish just standing near the rocks! Be careful of the cross currents near the Getty!  There are bathrooms and showers and picnic tables!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach with good sandy area for beginners
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This ended up being our favorite beach for snorkeling because of the large area of sand and "protected" area where waves were minimal. Had a large sea turtle come right up beside me and I followed it around for a while. Really fun. Great bathrooms and a shower, too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach and Snorkeling Time
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice relaxing beach that also has a small children’s play area. The swimming area is protected for those of us that like to float around. There’s also a lifeguard on site.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This place is great for kids. There are public toilets, a playground, parking and food right there. Water is calm and easy for small kids to go into. Kids enjoyed it a lot!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for families, easy surf, great snorkeling for young kids
reviewsWithKeywords.text: For families just starting out with snorkeling this is a great beach.  Easy surf where you can stand up in many locations.  There are plenty of colorful fish to see.  Make sure you bring some approved, safe fish food and you will have 50 fish around in minutes.  Caution: their are quite a few rocks, coral, and reef in the water so beware.  The beaches themselves a great with great sand.  Also, only reason I don't give this 5-stars is due to there being so many people there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We could walk here from our cottage. Restrooms and tables, Sunday was pretty crowded.Across the street is parking and Brenneckes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very nice for small kids
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed in a condo just steps away from here. There is a playground our 3 year old just loved.  We would come out after dinner to watch sunset and would let her run around.  We were watching turtles arriving at the beach tonight at sunset, there were at least 7 of them coming out, it was so cool.  Shaved ice or ice cream from the deli across the street on the way back. Very nice. Little kids are very safe in the little pool, protected by the rocks. Its literally knee deep for an average adult.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: An easy swimming beach with small sandy beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of hotels in the area and this is the main beach area so be prepared to be around lots of other folks. No big waves so easy in and out of the water

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach on the Island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Turtles swimming in the bay, clean and tidy, play area for kids and lots of grass for family gatherings.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for children
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We traveled from Southern California with our 5 yr old son. Big beach, nice snorkeling, easy for children. Restrooms, showers and picnic tables available. Some shade. Shaved ice a very short walk from beach. This is a beautiful beach that has many areas protected from waves, lots of lifeguard stations. We stopped by here a few times because we enjoyed it very much. Sea turtles and seals frequent here.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Protected beach with lifeguard
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The public beach is protected by a rock barrier in a half moon shape so that the breakers are more calm.  It is widely used and clean.  Picnic tables available.  Restaurant Across the street.  Lots of “feral” chickens to amuse all.  I’ve seen seals sunning on the beach there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great waves and fun people watching area
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went with our boys in 2013 we all enjoyed playing In The waves and watching the surfers and biggie boards too.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Awesome snorkeling!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Don't waste your time going any other place to snorkel!! We tried two other beaches with zero fish but Poipu beach was amazing. Teeming with all kinds of beautiful fish. If snorkeling is your thing this is the place!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach on Kauai!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was visiting Poipu beach in early September for snorkeling and have to say that it is the best beach that I have been to in Kauai!  It's fun to watch the surfers as the waves run sort of diagonal to the beach.  Fun, young crowd and I definitely want to come back as my visit was fairly short.Also, the northern part of the island gets a lot of rain which is good to know when you go to Queen's Bath. But they say that the southern island has up to 95% sunny days!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: May wife and I recently visited Poipu Beach Park. This is a beautiful place to visit, we actually had a very enjoyable and relaxing lunch just watching the waves and the birds - there were lots of hens running around too. This is well worth a stop while visiting Kauai.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sunset must see
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Went here for sunset to take pictures and video and it is beautiful! Rock and sand beach. Theres a ton of surfers too. There are signs there warning you about the tide pulls, be aware and stay closer to shore!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great family area, you can picnic, swim, snorkel with fish, see turtles swimming or laying on the beach,.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Right across the street
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved staying at the cat bird seat right across the street from this beautiful beach.The snorkeling was awesome. Sunsets are breath taking. This beach also has wild life come up and take a nap. A very popular beach with young children because it has an area that is protected by big lava rocks from the big waves.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I didn’t even need to put a toe in the water to enjoy this place! I rented a bike & landed at a shaded picnic table. I’m was content & at peace to watch the crashing waves & feel the gentle breeze. It was nice to watch people enjoy the shallow beach. What a nice place!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkeling, Sunsets, Sea Turtles!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I stayed at a bed & breakfast near here and let me tell you, it is one of the best swimmable beaches in Kauai!Snorkeling was great - lots of beautiful fish, sunsets were amazing (around 6:30PM is a good time to go), and my favorite....sea turtles coming up shore to sleep!!! Though they are super cute, please refrain from touching or bothering them. But feel free to admire these beautiful creatures that have traveled long and far to get some rest!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great place to take im the sun and snorkel!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great family friendly beach. It is a great place to snorkel.  Because if the shore break the water is calmer and there are a lot of fish.  With clean public restrooms, shelters and clean up showers. There is a life gaurd on duty for safety. Best snorkeling I found on the south side.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lots of snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of people, not over crowded. I would recommend wearing swim shoes since it is rocky near the shore.  Lots of rentals for gear.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach for a family
reviewsWithKeywords.text: One this beach, there is a very calm area, where we took our 1 1/2 year old grandchild.  There is also a portion with more surf and a spot to watch the more exciting surf.  The sandy beach is plenty wide for people to spread out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: What a lively beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great spot to snorkel(current can be strong and waves pretty heavy) but there is a little kids area where the water is no more then a foot and a half deep. You can snorkel along the rock wall and see heaps without being battered by waves. Or there is the main bay area but I highly recommend getting reef shoes as it’s very rocky/coral and with the current you will get pushed back and forth as you get in/out. We went there twice and saw a turtle on the beach each day with a Monk seal the second time. The shaved ice place across the road is just perfect after a day snorkeling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Cool snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Great spot to snorkel and see tropical fish in the reef. Parking was easy. Brennekes across the street has great fish tacos for lunch

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too crowded / commercial
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice to have the lifeguards but we preferred other beaches with way less people.  There is a large grassy are prior to the beach, so you can spread out, but definitely didn't have the "tropical island" / more remote feel for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Swam briefly watched people and left in about 1 hr
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed near this beach.  A lifeguard was getting a workout advising swimmers about rip currents etc as many seemed compelled to swim to a sand bar just off shore.  Lots of people here. Parking is in short supply about 10-11am.  Arrive early or wait for the first comers to leave at lunch to get a spot.  Refreshing swim.  Saw people snorkeling but I don’t think it is very good here as it is sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Turtles & Seals
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely beach with a sheltered area which provides a calm swimming area, but large surfing waves are close by. Large turtles and seals are frequently on the beach making this a unique site!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Stunning beach excellent snorkling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved the beach so much that in the 7 days we went 5 days. The beach is stunning blue, great sand and places that are not in the sun. Make this you place to go whether if it is for swimming, snorkeling and perfect for families also.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice, swimmable beach, good snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park and beach are very nice, there are calm enough areas even for the youngest visitors, up to nice surfing areas. We saw monk seals and sea turtles basking in the sun several days, really special to see. Snorkeling right off the beach is very good, there's a lot of coral, footwear of some sort is highly recommended. There are lifeguard stands regularly spaced and they do a good job of notifying you of surf changes and guiding you to the safest areas. The park has nice areas to shower after swimming and many picnic areas, a playground for the kids, and equipment/chair rentals just across the street. Great area for just about any beach activity.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great swimming and snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice. Kids area too without much wave action. Easy walk from our condo and all amenities right there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: A beautiful beach and a nice place for sunsets
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park is grass with sand near the water. The water is highly protected, making swimming very nice. Snorkeling isn't half bad. There are restroom facilities and a lovely area for the keiki to play.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Calm Crowded Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: It's a very nice spot for a beach day with toddlers. It does get crowded and parking can be a hassle. Expect those hurdles and you'll have a fun day at this beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved it!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved our time at Poipu! We set up our towels under a palm tree, rented snorkel masks from Nukumoi Surf Shop for only $4 per person for the day, and had the best time! It was Labor Day but it wasn't as crowded as we thought it'd be. We swam out to the little island and there was a monk seal & a sea turtle resting on the beach - we stayed 20 feet away as instructed by the lifeguard, but it was so cool to be so close to them! There are bathrooms in the grassy area & a free parking lot across the street. There is also a great little area for kids to swim in, it's shielded from the rest of the ocean by rocks. We would definitely go back!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Wonderful Snorkeling and Amazing Blowhole...
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great first time snorkeling beach. The water is swimmable and the fish are plentiful. Be sure to check out the blowhole.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great kids beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: A must visit if you have young children. Great kids beach with protected beach area, playground, ramadas, life guards, fish, and animals to watch sun bathing on the beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great spot including for entry level snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Always nice to arrive at an Hawaiian beach for the first time and be greated by a monk seal.Great little beach and a great spot to snorkel, especially for younger children learning as they can still stand where they will see plenty of fish.I taught our 5yr old to snorkel here and the excitement he had from it will stay with me for a life time.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: World class beach park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: When you arrive first time to this beach park it seems as a nirmally beach park, but when you decide to go there, swimming or snorkling you discover that this beach park is something special. If you are lucky you will see monk seal, sea turtle and a lot of fantastic fish even when you snokel close to the beach. It is amazing. Lifeguards on duty and good restroom. Access to the water is good even without beach shoes

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beaches
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The park area is well maintained. We were there it was somewhat busy but lots of beach to enjoy. The waves were great for body surfing but still low enough to swim without too much trouble. Nice drive to get there.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice beach, snorkeling & wildlife
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a nice beach area with adequate parking and bathrooms/showers. Shallow, sheltered area for little kids. We had great snorkeling here. Lots of fish and a good environment even for beginner snorkelers. We rented gear from Boss Frog next to Lawai Beach. Went to Poipu Beach to snorkel several times during our trip. Saw sea turtles &/or sea lions every time. It can get busy but there is plenty of room for everyone.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Simple, easy snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: If you’re okay with the crowds, and sharing the water with several knee-highs, this is a super easy spot to introduce your very own tiny person to the wonderful world of ocean snorkeling. There are fish present pretty much as you step into the water (you should enter towards the very left of the beach - all sand makes it a very easy runway), and the number of species on display only increase the further out you venture.We came here a few days when the weather was bad, to be guaranteed low surf, visibility was still decent despite the rain, and we even ran into a trio of sea turtles in the shallow waters. Oh yeh, monk seals too!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great beach for sunning and snorkeling.  I saw many beautiful fish and a large sea turtle.  Restaurants and beach rental supplies across the street.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great family beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Excellent for families and beginning surfers. Cheap surf lessons are close by and the weather is always superb!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach park good for swimming families and picnics.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My husband and I visited for the day and we found a great spot under a palm tree to relax and enjoy the ocean breeze.  This beach is good for swimming and people of all ages. It has amenities plus areas to picnic. We stayed in Kapaa and took an Uber to this beach. (About 50 us each way). Stop in Koloa if you can it’s really a cute town. Also luxury shopping and dining nearby at a shopping center. Right across from the beach is a deli for drinks and sandwiches. A very worthwhile trip.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkling Paradise!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: An amazingly clear area to snorkel.  We were fortunate to see a sea turtle.  The coral is very rough and water shoes are a must!  Restaurants right around the corner!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for beginner snorkelers
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a great beach for beginning snorkelers and little kid boogie boarding.  There is a life guard, so you know you got back up if something goes wrong.We saw lots of fish, a Monk Seal on the beach and a sea turtle on the beach.  it was a busy beach.  Parking is convenient, but fills up by about 10-11 am.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Pretty Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach was a little crowded but having lifeguards and a very controlled environment was nice.  Snorkeling is good, with lots of fish. I think this is a lovely beach :)

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded but loved the seals
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Pros: seals sunning on the beach, lots of chickens running around, restrooms, showers, covered picnic tables, lifeguard, great access for small children all the way to the left side.Cons: very crowded, hard to get in the water to snorkel unless you go to the kiddie side, lots of rocks rather than sand underfoot, not many fish to see compared to other beaches, strong current, very small swimming area, not a lot of room to boogie board, parking area is small. Didn’t live up to the hype for us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Lovely views with snorkeling🌴
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We spent a long afternoon here and enjoyed the waves, water and snorkeling. Great family beach. Perfect place for beach yoga, as well!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: If you want to see sea turtles on beach and fishes, this is where you need to go
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu beach is very close to our hotel.  We get to visit the beach twice, once for snorkeling where you actually see fishes and it is not too deep.  Part of the beach is semi-circled by some rocks which reduce waves make it safe for kids to play around and its only waist deep.If you want to see sea turtles chilling on the beach, this is where you go.  We saw two turtles on the beach chilling at around 6AM in the morning.  Yup, 6AM.  I guess that is when the beach is less crowded.  Make sure you keep your distances from the turtles ( there is signs on the beach asking you to keep your distances).  When we got there, someone draw some circles 10 ft around the turtles.  Not sure who draw that, maybe the life guards or some animal agency?  Either way, if you spot them on beach, don't disturb their hang-loose time...

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Very Pleasant
reviewsWithKeywords.text: lots of praking, lots of sand.  some fish for snorkeling but not as many as Lawai.  we saw monk seals on the beach one evening which was very cool.  Nice beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Warm and calm water, good snorkeling, easy cleanup after.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Covered pools make this fun for those who are not into open water! Snorkeling here was awesome...saw a ton of fish (lots of angel fish and a lot that I do not know the name of--they do have a chart that you can check on). Strong shower to clean off of after your saltwater swim/snorkeling fun!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Search for Sea turtles and monk seal
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was on a mission to see the majestic sea turtle on our visit to the island. After doing a bit of research I found the best place to see them without snorkeling is on Poipu Beach. Sure enough after a short stroll from the parking lot across from Brennecks there they were lounging on the sand! A few feet away there were even Monk seals napping! This is overall a very beautiful beach, I would definitely want to snorkel here my next visit.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: No visit to the South side is complete without grabbing a deli sandwich from Brenekes and then hitting the beach. There is limited sand space when you park out front the sandy stretch of beach in front of the houses and the Marriott, but that's okay, the water is easy to get into and you can snorkel, float in a tube, swim over to the little sand island or sunbathe. It can get extremely hot if there is full sun, so be prepared. There is usually a Hawaiian Monk Seal to greet you or a Green Sea Turtle to swim next to. Who doesn't love that. It's great for kids to!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Loved snorkeling here
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a fun beach to snorkel! The fish here are apparently so used to people (and being fed by people) that they come right up and surround you which makes for some fun snorkeling! The current was a bit strong outside of the "baby beach" area, so I recommend making sure you're a confident swimmer before venturing out. While we were there, 3 monk seals swam right through the protected cove where everyone was snorkeling and decided to sunbathe on the beach with the tourists. It was an incredible sight. My only complaint is that the beach is VERY crowded. Otherwise totally worth the trip!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good Snorkeling But Too Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach had the best snorkeling during our trip, but was very crowded. We saw so much sea life, including a huge turtle, but you are constantly trying to avoid getting kicked by another snorkeler.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Its Hawaii at its more relaxing
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved my experiences in Poipu so much I want to move there!!  The sunsets are breathtaking.  The sea life in the water is amazing!!! Snorkel, swim, walk along the water... and your troubles seem to melt away.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Special Adventure
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I like be to snorkel. This beach is easy to get to on the south shore of Kauai.. we make Kauai our #1 destination every summer with Poipu Beach first on the list.. From warm crystal clear water, filled with an abundance or tropical marine life of all kinds.. Monk Seals seem to be on display along with one of the biggest sea turtles you'll find up close.. Enjoy this Special Adventure!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is very big beach park. There is a lot of shade (big trees) to hide from the sun and it is family friendly. There are restroom facilities and a lot of benches and tables to have a picnic. There are also showers. The sea is easily accessible and the current is not too strong. There is a small island off the beach to which you can walk through the water where are monk seals usually resting. You are not allow to come too near (you can disturb them). If you do you are kindly warned from the lifeguards at the beach with loud horn. Be very careful and do not walk to close to the edge of the island. The waves on the other side are sometimes very high and they can swipe you off. That portion of the island is made of magma rocks and it is very dangerous to fall. Right on the beach you can also come across big turtles.There are a few parking lots with a lot of parking spaces but at the weekends you have to try very hard to find the empty one.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Da best snorkeling.  Small crowds.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lovely large variety of delightful sea life. Neighborhood park great for picnics and playi ng small and large group games.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: great place to sun bathe or swim
reviewsWithKeywords.text: guarded by a life guard, and with a shallow area for the little ones, this beach and ocean are for all members of your family.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Delightful
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this beach! It was beautiful, not too crowded and we saw a Monk Seal, which was an added bonus.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The beach features a protected area to the left and right that's still and fairly shallow for young kids. You can even see some tropical fish while swimming.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sand bar has gone
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We we're here 2 years ago and there were 2 back to back crescents of sand leading out to a rocky outcrop. That sandbar is no longer there, washed out by a storm and they have no idea when it will return. So it's not the beach it was but still has good snorkeling and is safe for kids most times of the year and has a life guard.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really nice beach....
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I like that the boogie boards are on a separate part of beach, and swimmers tend to stay towards the center. There are waves, but with the jetty’s where they are, it seems to temper them a little- but still watch the rip tide. It is shallow and doesn’t drop off quickly like many other beaches....you can even walk/swim to a spit of sand out a little ways which was cool too....Nice beach to relax at as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We found this beach to be very crowded and not all that attractive, relative to other nearby beaches.  I'm sure it's an attraction because the swimming is relatively safe and it's easy to access.  There is a very pretty protected cove for small children - much too shallow for our six year old.  On the other end of the beach, in front of the hotel, is a larger sandy area that is still very crowded with families - and we went early (8 am).  The beach has a grassy area with bathrooms and a small play area for children.  I can see how it would be convenient for large families, but we weren't fans.  Wouldn't return.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Crowded and cluttered sand
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach is extremely popular because of all the resorts in the area, so it is very crowded, both in an out of the water.  The sand is full of sticks, leaves, etc. If you are looking for a peaceful, secluded spot, this is not the place.  There are many more beaches on Kauai to explore.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We visited Poipu daily on our trip to Kauai.  In the mornings we saw sea turtles and occasionally seals.  There is a calm, shallow area for young children to swim, and waves farther up for boogie boarding and surfing.  There is a swing set and there are showers to rinse off.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Popular and fun beach!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: While it can get pretty crowded, Poipu Beach is a classic spot on Kauai! It is beautiful at all hours, especially at sunset! If you get hungry, Brenecke's deli has great sandwiches and breakfast food!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Fantastic Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water here was relatively calm for swimming and also snorkeling.  We saw various types of fish here and even some seals!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellent beach for small children, and good snorkelling for older ones
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a small, very sheltered beach which is excellent for small children. In the slightly deeper waters there is very good snorkelling, with quite a range of species close to shore. Occasionally turtles will appear in the water and on the sand, but not as many as some other locations.There is shade, although get there early to make sure you get it. Plenty of grass, good changing rooms and observant life guards. Occasionally it can become quite busy, especially on weekends, but there is a good vide and strong family atmosphere.Across the road is a good burger, snack, shave ice store and there is plenty of parking as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sheltered swimming spot
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Such a lovely spot to swim in the ocean but to have some shelter from the waves at Poipu ocean, water was nice and clear so when snorkeling you can see the fish swimming, the change rooms are clean and the park tables are clean life guards on duty and there’s a niceDeli across the road which also has a bar upstairs for a sit down meal

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great for little kids in addition to adults- seals and turtles also like it
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We stayed at Koa Kea Resort which was a 5 minute walk on the beach to get to Poipu Beach.  We had a lot of fun hear seeing the turtle come on the beach to rest two days in a row, we also saw two seals playing for at least two hours.   Lifeguards made sure people stayed 20 feet way to avoid issues with the seals who were swimming around us.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful but crowded beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach to walk, swim, boogie board, etc. The amount of sand space is limited however and it was a crowded summer day. The views to the east are spectacular, where you can watch the waves crashing against the faraway cliffs. We chose to sit at the comfort of the bar and grill at the Marriott for lunch. We had a tasty fish sandwich with fries. Definitely recommend this beach for activity, but not if you want serenity and privacy.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Must See!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Of all the beaches here on Kauai, Poipu is one you’ll want to visit and revisit. Plan to spend all day, bring chairs, goggles, snorkel gear, snacks, drinks, and plenty of sunblock. The kids love it!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Family Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Nice beach area but you have to come early to find parking.  We got there at 9:30, and the parking lot was almost full.  Beach was nice and clean but very busy.  We saw a tortoise and some seals come ashore for a while.  That was really neat. The park area had a lot of playground equipment and picnic tables.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Much smaller than I thought, and quite crowded
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We drove along the south coast stopping at a number of sightseeing stops. I was looking forward to this beach to see the tombolo (the peninsula of sand that separates the beach into two). Unfortunately, we were there at high tide, so it wasn't that prominent. The beach was smaller than I expected and very crowded. We managed to get a parking spot across the street, but we didn't bother staying to swim as it was just too crowded. It does look like the left side of the beach (as you facing the ocean) would be ideal for little kids as it was quite shallow for paddling.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Body surfing beach fun, but be careful of rocks in spots
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My family visit Kaui in July and had a blast on the west side of the island at Poipu Beach. The water is always warm, there was public parking, and much body sufing to be had. We spent the whole day there. We were told by locals to go more by the Sheraton resort for a nice beach area, but we did stop along multiple spots on other days as well. (By the Sheraton was the best, and I would recommend staying in that area for your Kaui visit). The water was rougher than normal producing bigger waves for this time of year due to a Hurricane out in the waters a ways away. We did not snorkel however this is the spot we were told to go if we wanted to as well. There seems to be rocks at most of the beaches around the island and I have to say yes there are some but not horrible, just be aware of them.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach but Very Rocky
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a beautiful beach to snorkel, but it's crowded and extremely rocky. You definitely need water shoes and to watch where you are stepping.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Good Snorkeling
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We went to a lot of different beaches that I had seen were supposed to have good snorkeling for families and were disappointed with all of them.  This was the one beach we went to that had clear water and lots of fish to see and it was right next to our hotel so it was perfect.  Each day we went there was a sea turtle laying on the sand for part of the day before it returned to the water.  The kids got to see a lot of different kinds of fish and enjoyed just swimming and playing in the water as well.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach, good for families and young kids as well as surfers and snorkelers.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good sandy beach, restroom facilities. There are many fish to see in the area, and occasional turtles and monk seals. There are also areas with decent waves for the surfers and boogie boarders to try out. The Poipu area is very scenic and beautiful, great for a short visit or a longer leisurely stay anytime!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The water was great and lifeguards kept everyone safe.  While there we could snorkel and see all kinds of fish.  The endangered monk seals were there and well protected by volunteers.  The sea turtle was even there one day.  The  beach was so beautiful.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach, gorgeous views.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved visiting this beach.  Only had a little time before our plane departed, so our visit was short.  Tons of fish to see.  Saw two different types of eels as well.  While the waves were pretty big out front, the pool area was pretty easy to snorkel in and felt safe.  Many people were body boarding to the west along the beach and that looked great as well.   Probably saw the most and the largest variety of fish here so close to the shore out of the 8+ beaches were visited.  Was the busiest by far though of those beaches.  But it was not crowded.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Excellant Beach.
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Clean sand. A little crowded by noon. Needs more parking. Lots fill up fast. Nice area for kids, about 24 - 30 inches deep with a lava breakwater to cut down the waves and currents. Go a little farther down for more waves and snorkeling. From there, about 50 yards out, sand bar island you can get to. Couple life guard stations. Nice beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Snorkeling Is Nice
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Lots of opportunity to watch people.  The water is nice and their are fish to see.  Easy to park.  Don't forget the sunscreen.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Really Nice Beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice beach with many things to do. There is a shallow and black by the rocks which does not get many currents. Further off the beach there is an open area which gets deep and has many currents. We saw a few monk seals up close and personal.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Best beach on the island
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Staying at the Waiohai we were on this beach daily and were able to see seals, turtles, and even a stingray.  Great family friendly beach.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Amazing wildlife!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: I was amazed at the wildlife at this beach in the water and on the sand considering the number of people who are on the beacj at any given time. The snorkeling was the best we found on the island and it was just off the beach. The first time we visited the beach in the morning we saw one monk seal; the next morning there were 3 along with a turtle on the sand.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This in my opinion is the best beach in Kauai. Lifeguards are present, calm waters. And you may even see a monk seal swim up on the beach. Parking can be a problem on the weekend

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beach Day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Spent 2 days on Poipu Beach.Beautiful beach with some good snorkeling. Both days there got to see monk seals and sea turtles.They were a wonder to experience.The Beach itself wasn’t too crowded.There is a restaurant within 100 yards Beach has lifeguards.Water shoes a plus lot a volcanic rock in water. Would recommend spending a day on Poipu Beach

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great public beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Very nice public beach area. Our hotel was a ten minute walk down the beach so we came here several timesI was able to see sea turtles resting on the sand on multiple days. We also saw Hawaiian Monk Seals. One day two seals were playing in the shallow water - wrestling, flipping, and having funYou could do a short walk through water to get to a sand bar if you can dare the rocks and the surf. It is easy in water shoes but a little tough in bare feet. There is a nice deli across the street for lunch.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Perfect Poipu beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a HUGE beach area with a large wide expanse of grass also.  There are picnic tables, some under pavilions, and two lifeguard stations that are staffed until 5pm daily.  You can usually see Hawaiian monk seals and/or sea turtles beached on the sand for hours each day.  Roped off areas around the sea lions keep the public at a safe distance to let the animals rest.  The beach has some sandy areas for entering the water, but there are large underwater coral/rock areas that make entering difficult.  There can be strong currents that don't allowing snorkelers to go in the best area for seeing many fish.  Lifeguards make swimmers aware of the currents and continually try to keep people out of those areas.  There is a keiki beach area where it is better for children - sandy, more shallow water, situated in more of a "bay" area of the beach.  A bit further down the beach in front of the hotels is the surfing area - sometimes big waves attract lots of surfers.  Boogie boarders can also be found there as well as to the north of the main Poipu beach area where the waves are also quite big.  There is parking across the street and up and down the main road.  There are no concessions here, but there is a restaurant/bar across the road as well as a small deli.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Always a nice day
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Sunshine and medium crowds made for a nice visit. There were two monk seals on the beach which drew quite a crowd. Great snorkeling spot and swimming for all ages with two lifeguard stations.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach - watch out for the chickens
reviewsWithKeywords.text: We loved this beach.  It was beautiful - we walked out to the "island" and looked at the sea lions sleeping.  They are so cute!  Snorkeling is great!  Water is so clear - just have to be careful where you enter as it can be a bit rocky and lots of coral close to shore.  There were chickens just walking around on the beach and they will get into your food if you have anything laying out.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Spectacular coast
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Poipu was by far my favorite side of Kauai.  Poipu beach is a Must see. The foliage is so colorful and lush.  The water is a gorgeous blue and the homes along this coast are gorgeous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Little something for all
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The currents are fairly strong here so weak swimmers be cautious, otherwise a fun and lots to offer beach.Lifeguards are on hand and a free car park and nice deli close by for sandwiches and quick bites.The sealife is colorful  and plentiful  but there are some sharp rocks and coral in parts.Very enjoyable.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Big waves
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This was a beautiful place that would be good for surfing or using a boogie board because the waves were pretty boisterous.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Nice Beach!!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: t’s a nice beach. You can go snorkeling, swimming. The water temperature was perfect! Not too hot & too cold! Just right! Nice soft sand.  There’s a few lifeguards there. There’s picnic tables. Perfect for family, friends who want to get together & have a picnic with Oceanfront Views!!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Place to watch Turtles
reviewsWithKeywords.text: My wife and I were there about 9:00 am and we were able to see several sea turtles. You can clearly see themJust under the water and then they stick their heads up so be ready for your picture. They had heads up about 3 seconds at a time. Funny thing is the scuba folks were on one end of the cove and the turtles were in the middle. One of our resort friends said they watch turtles about every afternoon around 6 pm. Awesome sight. Their is public parking lot on the east end.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Great Beach for boogie boarding
reviewsWithKeywords.text: The waves were a little high in May for snorkeling, so make sure to be a strong swimmer when venturing in cloudy weather. The boogie boarding is fun.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Number one beach on the island!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Loved this park! Great snorkeling with a golden sand color. They have showers to wash sand off. There are picnic tables so stop and get lunch before you go.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: This gem was right outside our resort doors
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This beach had it all for our family. Sunrise and sunsets, turtles sleeping on the sand beach, monk seals to entertain us with their antics, amazing snorkeling in the lava "reef", boogie boarding. What a gem! All under the supervision of lifeguards with running water for showers and drinking. This is a not to be missed place on Kauai!

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful beach
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Our family (4 total) spent a week in Kauai and had a great time at Poipu Beach.  A great place to just relax and chill.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Beautiful and big Beach Park
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Conveniently located for residents at Poipu Kai.It’s a big beach park with showers and bathrooms.It’s divided in 2 parts, a soft sandy baby beach with gentle waves and great snorkeling.It’s right next to Brennecke beach, home of boogies boarding or surfing.Surrounded by 4 big names chain hotels, Sheraton, Marriott, Grand Hyatt and the Poipu Kai resort.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Sea turtles everywhere!
reviewsWithKeywords.text: This is a great place to bring the kids to snorkel. Marine life plentiful, though sometimes the water can be murky due to swimmers (and maybe the amount of sunblock?). We went there on different days, and on the days we went, we always saw a turtle on the beach sunbathing. One time, we even swam with a turtle for over 15 minutes.  Great place for families.

reviewsWithKeywords.title: Too crowded, but nice on off times
reviewsWithKeywords.text: Good snorkeling offshore when the waves aren't too big. We saw plenty of fish, turtles, and a monk seal. Signs say there are common rip tides, so not ideal for beginners. Summertime swells make the currents and waves bigger, but there's some protected waters for younger children to play in. There's also surf rentals nearby, so this becomes a popular spot for tourists and locals. Parking is limited on weekends and the narrow stretch of beach can be densely packed. Plenty of less crowded beaches nearby that are nicer.

reviews.title: Amazing turtle experience!
reviews.text: We had heard that there were a number of sea turtles coming ashore every evening, so we decided to check it out.  We did not expect 30+ huge individuals.As we watched, they continued to come ashore.   Very quick until they hit the sand - then you could see the struggle.  Simply amazing.  Area around the turtles was marked off with red tape.  People were very respectful. Plenty of parking available along the street.

reviews.title: Beautiful area
reviews.text: We stopped this beach while touring Kauai.  The weather wasn’t very nice to swimming wasn’t really an option, although it looked like it would be a nice spot in the right conditions.  The waves were quite large outside of the cove.  This highlight were the turtles.  There were at least 25-30 large turtles resting on the beach.  That’s the most we’ve seen in any one place.  This area is definitely worth visiting.

reviews.title: So many turtles!!
reviews.text: When we got to the beach midday there were 18 turtles on the beach. We decided to drive back to our nearby hotel to grab our snorkeling gear. Came back and there were 40 turtles on the beach. Incredible!!

reviews.title: Crowd-central
reviews.text: While this is certainly a scenic spot, the crowds we experienced over the holidays made it unpleasant. It might be better in the low season. Parking was tough and it was like being at a concert in terms of crowds.

reviews.title: The sleeping turtles are magical
reviews.text: This beach was lovely to watch the sunrise and get to experience the nightly/early rotation of sea turtles who call that beach their home outside the water. *As a friendly reminder for all that go to see the turtles and other wildlife there… please don’t act entitled. There are beautiful kind volunteers who give their time to protect the turtles space. This is for THEIR safety. Don’t be rude to them, if they tell you that you are too close (walking inside their cone barriers) politely apologize and step back. They don’t deserve to be yelled at. They are doing the work so we can to view and be in company of amazing animals. It breaks my heart to witness tourists who think they are entitled to a picture so close to the animal and then yell at the volunteers who politely ask them to step away. Use your camera zoom and don’t be a jerk please!

reviews.title: Awesome Day
reviews.text: We had an awesome time on the beach areas. In hindsight, you could park at the main parking area and hit several locations along the Poipu Beach area. You can swim, boogie board, and see the turtles all in one day. I don't recommend eating near the beach because it is very expensive. Take snacks and treat yourself to an early dinner in  Old Koloa Town.

reviews.title: Best beach on Kauai ...
reviews.text: Super easy to walk to. Plenty of space to set your chair down and enjoy a morning, afternoon or day at the beach. Surf is good for young kids to play and more than good enough for great boogy boarding or body surfing. Spot the sea turtles in the surf or at sunset check them and seals out on the beach. If you have patience, scan the ocean horizon, you will definitely see whale activity ... Spouts, tails and breeching. Enjoy!!!

reviews.title: Turtles everywhere, just amazing
reviews.text: A great place to see the Hawaii green Sea turtles. They are all around and just napping on the beach among people. Its a beautiful and large beach with plenty of space to hangout with the turtles.

reviews.title: Best beach of the south shore of the island
reviews.text: One of the best beaches on the island. Great mix of beach, wild life, surf. What is special are the 20+ turtles who come swim out on the beach. We Sally see sea lions but not this time. Only tough part of the beach - tough to get in and out of the water due to the rocks

reviews.title: Love
reviews.text: Turtles, waves, sun, sand, boogie boarding, and all within walking distance of several hotels and condominiums available for rent.

reviews.title: 10/10 Would Recommend
reviews.text: Such a great beach to watch the turtles. There were lots of people but it didnt feel crowded. Also a great place to catch the sunset.

reviews.title: Go For The Turtles!
reviews.text: This popular beach is located in the south part of Kauai. It is known for being a beautiful beach with great swimming. There are two lifeguard stands staffed with lifeguards. There is ample parking which is not always a thing with some of the beaches on Kauai. Our favorite thing about this beach is when the green sea turtles come up on shore to rest. It is quite a site to see. The area around the turtles is protected by a series of cones with signs telling visitors to stay back and to leave the turtles alone. While we were there, everyone was very respectful and did not cross the boundary.The beach is clearly marked from the main road and easy to find. There is a restaurant right on the beach so if you need something to eat or drink, you can do so without having to leave.

reviews.title: Aloha
reviews.text: The turtles were so amazing - they come up to sleep every night. Any where from 1-50- not joking!!! Be respectful. Across the street is puka dogs, it was yummy

reviews.title: Well designed beach park with something for all ages!
reviews.text: Quite a lovely place with grass, covered picnic area & water  suitable for toddlers up to snorklers!  We were staying almost next door at Waiohai Beach Club so it was a 5 minute beach stroll from our home base, often  strewn with monk seals and green sea turtles every day of our stay. Visitors were respecting the resting wild life and the dedicated volunteers were kept busy by the frequently moving turtles and seals. The most turtles seen at one time by various family members were 72 sea turtles after sunset one evening!  In the early hours after 7AM,  usually only a few, but Brenneke’s coffee and bakery shop across the street is open early for pleasant beach snack at the picnic benches.

reviews.title: Great Place To Eat Your Puka Dog On The Beach
reviews.text: We sat at one of the picnic benches in this park to eat our Puka Dog, which I highly recommend.  There is a big pavilion and picnic tables scattered around.  Most have shade, so do not. We had no issue grabbing a table this time of year.  We sat and ate and enjoyed the sounds of ocean for about 25 minutes. There is a playground for kids and a public restroom also available.  The beach itself was not to crowded considering to is in close proximity to lots of hotels & resorts. We were there early afternoon so we missed the turtles coming up onto the beach.  You could see where they rope off for the turtles to try to keep tourist from getting to close.We did find an old pay phone booth that still had the phones in the booth! I thought that was pretty fun!  The park itself is nice, the beach is beautiful but busy.  We did walk to the other side of the beach where it was very rocky.  Also beautiful here.

reviews.title: Sunsets and turtles amidst white sand and clear waters
reviews.text: One of my favorite beaches in Kauai. This is one of the best places to see the sunset if you’re near the south or eastern side of Kauai. If you come during sunset, you’ll get a chance to see the sea turtles come with the waves to rest for the evening. Although you can’t get close to them, you can go snorkeling in the water just don’t touch the animals. If you have any questions about them, there are local volunteers protecting and answering any questions people have about the turtles.Also, there is a parking lot across the street so come early to find the best parking. During sunset besides turtles, you’ll see surfers, riding the waves. One of the best sunsets of my life.

reviews.title: Great Beach and Water Aerobics Class
reviews.text: Love this beach. Great soft sand. A great place to see turtles and monk seals. There is nothing better than getting your beach chairs and parasol and relaxing on the beach. Great to watch the surfers. The ocean is so warm and a great place to cool off. However the best for me is Charlotte’s water aerobics class in the ocean held on Tuesday, Thursday and Saturday mornings at 9am.

reviews.title: Snorkeling and Turtles!
reviews.text: Loved this beach. It had excellent snorkeling from the beach. Lots of colorful fish. Also when we were there, there were lots of turtles on land. It was cool to see them. We went mid-morning and didnt have a problem finding parking. They do have bathrooms but they were quite disgusing.

reviews.title: People are indifferent and cruel towards animals
reviews.text: We were there today and it was honestly kind of disgusting how people were acting around the beach. They seemed to be keeping an okay distance from the turtles and there were several volunteers answering questions. My main concern here is that we witnessed someone run over and kill a young chicken. They immediately left and it had seizures/convulsions(?) until it died. We told a shop owner and he said no one cares about the chickens. Our waiter at dinner told us not to mourn the chicken and that it didn’t matter at all. Probably 30 minutes later, we saw 4 people put a rooster into a garbage can and shake it until the rooster starting crying.

reviews.title: Bring water shoes, trust me, it will make your experience so much nicer
reviews.text: If I could offer one piece of advise, its to BRING WATER SHOES.  I'm so glad we had them in the car.  The entrance into the water is rocky with lots of divots. I observed lots of people entering the water with their arms spread, trying to balance themselves from falling.    Once we put on the water shoes, it was a lot easier to get in.    The water was crystal clear and the snorkeling is fantastic.  I saw more fish here than I saw on our snorkeling expedition.  There are 2 lifeguards who are continuously telling people to "not mess with the wildlife" and to move in closer".  I felt super safe here.   When we were here, there was a large turtle who was making its way to the beach.

reviews.title: Great beach but watch out for theft
reviews.text: Beautiful snorkeling beach.  Tons of fish, pretty shallow water.  Park has lifeguards, restrooms, showers, a playground and plenty of free parking.  The issue is we were robbed. There is a concrete wall in the back of the park, its guarding a cemetery.  We put our two bags next to the wall and when we came back our bookbag was taken and rummaged through. Our bag was dropped a short distance away. We didn't have anything of value in our bags but you have to be careful of this area even on a busy beach day.   Just a reminder to leave valuables at home or in the car and enjoy this beautiful beach.  🤙

reviews.title: Great amenities and beautiful beaches
reviews.text: The beach was beautiful. It’s a park with amenities, so expect more of a crowd than other beaches in Kauai. We tried snorkeling but there were others who had the same idea. We enjoyed lounging on the beach and listening to the waves.Look for the green turtles who are sunbathing. They are in a protected area and easy to find.

reviews.title: Amazing day at the beach
reviews.text: Poipu beach is one of Kauai's south beaches! Dry and sunny all day. It's nestled with resorts and condos. Parking is fantastic and free, close to the beach. The park has showers to clean off the sand and bathroom. It also has picnic shelters. Thinner beaches with lifeguards, the beach drops off and has rocks all over. The current is dangerous so please listen to the lifeguards.

reviews.title: Cozy, family friendly and easily accessible
reviews.text: Small but popular, wonderful beach with golden sugar-soft sand. Unique touch are the sea turtles and monk seals who occasionally rest here- we saw both! For these reasons it drew me back for multiple visits- the easily accessible parking also helps. The signs carefully mark where the safe areas to swim are; there are powerful currents not too far so beware especially with children. The snorkeling is not bad (especially with the turtles), but the waves and surf can make it a little challenging.

reviews.title: Great beach with turtles and snorkelling opportunities, but watch the currents!
reviews.text: This was a nice family beach where turtles come and  sunbathe. It has life guards and they are on the ball looking after peoples safety with changing tides and strong currents. There are covered / shaded picnic tables, toilets and changing rooms and a free car park nearby.  There are coral reefs where people can snorkel and see tropical fish. The currents are strong so you need to be a competent swimmer and use fins. Big Al’s top tipsIf snorkelling come in the morning as the water is clearer and less murky. Use fins as the currents can be strong A good place to see turtles and free car parking toilet / changing rooms . One of the nicest beaches on the island and well worth a visit. Follow me for more travel tips around the world.

reviews.title: Pretty Views at Poipu Beach Park
reviews.text: If you're staying on the south side of Kaua'i, you will be familiar with Poipu Beach Park by day one.  It's a public beach with many places to relax, rocky points to search for sea life, and all around incredible views (especially those sunsets).If you're looking for a more private beach, this won't be it as it's a public beach for locals and tourists alike.

reviews.title: Beautiful, fun beach with sea turtles!
reviews.text: The beach was beautiful and there were at least 6 sea turtles on the beach in the late afternoon. There is a rock cove that is protected from the surf so you can swim and snorkel without worrying about the stronger tide.

reviews.title: Disappointed
reviews.text: Way crowded and rough waters. The rocky ocean floor tore up my kids' feet and knees. We literally left bloody. Apparently there are 2 sides to this beach - the one for surfing and the one for families. Yes, we were on the correct, calmer side. It was awful. The good thing about this beach is there are clean bathrooms and changing rooms.

reviews.title: Nice big beach park
reviews.text: I have been here many times to watch turtles and to swim. The calm side of the beach is usually pretty crowded - especially when the turtles are arriving or sleeping.
